prompt:
사용자 요청 원문:
좋아. 이제 인스턴스를 다시 켜고 첫 태스크를 만들어보자.
필요한 CLI 인증부터 확인하고, 로봇 조립·데이터센터 정비 분야에서 산업 근거가 있고 기존 제출과 겹치지 않는 후보를 골라 제출 전 검토 단계까지 진행해줘.

확정된 제작 조건:
- Category: Impact on AI timelines. 로봇 조립 또는 데이터센터 정비 중 실제 산업에서 자동화할 의미가 있는 물리 조작 하나를 선택한다.
- 제조사 설치·정비 매뉴얼, 공식 조립 절차, 공개 설계, 실제 작업 영상·보고서의 원문으로 작업과 장비 형상·치수·절차를 입증한다. 추측이나 가상 산업 용도를 만들어내지 않는다.
- 여러 후보를 비교하고 목적·물리 기술·성공 조건의 신규성과 로봇의 어려운 조작 능력을 함께 검토하여 하나만 제작한다. 조작의 어려움은 극단적일 필요는 없지만 단순 물체 옮기기를 산업 이름만 바꾼 작업은 피한다.
- 모든 분야의 기존 accepted/pending/open 제출 및 우리 팀 기존 제출, 지정된 기존 벤치마크와 비교한다. 기하·색상·배치·시작 자세·난도만 다른 것은 새 태스크가 아니다. 선정 시점 및 완성 후 다시 전수 비교한다. 불확실한 중복을 통과시키지 않는다.
- 가능한 강체 PhysX 작업을 선택한다. 기존의 검증된 연성 에셋이 없다면 새 연성 솔버 연구는 하지 않는다. 실제 산업 장비의 형태와 중요한 물리 제약을 재현한다. 공개 에셋은 라이선스·출처·치수를 기록하고 적합하지 않으면 직접 제작한다.
- objective와 환경·부품 물리를 먼저 완성·진단한 뒤 YAM 전체 데모·채점기를 연결한다. 물체 순간이동/상태 덮어쓰기로 성공을 만들지 않는다. 관련 부품 파손·금지 동작·실패·부분 점수와 성공 유지 시간을 수치로 평가한다.
- 실제 simulator 측정·두 번의 full-score YAM 데모·실패/부분 점수 대조군·영상/원시 trace 및 깨끗한 경로 재현 검사를 수행한다. 미검증 수치와 성공을 만들어 보고하지 않는다.
- 모든 제작·검증을 마친 후에만 Dream 최종 평가 episode 1회. 실패나 불명 결과도 자동 재평가하지 않는다. 누적 $20 ledger를 준수하고 인증이 없으면 제작을 보존한 뒤 평가 대기한다.
- 결과는 이 run의 새로운 origin 브랜치에 보존한다. 원본 매뉴얼 전체/인증 정보는 공개하지 않는다. 50MB/file 또는 100MB checkpoint 초과는 먼저 보고한다.
- 완료 후 GPU를 stop하고 제출 전 검토 보고서·영상·채점 결과를 제공한다. 실제 미디어 업로드·대회 PR·승인은 하지 않는다.
- 기존 feature/close-snack-bag checkout 및 robocurve-snack-film 인스턴스는 별개 작업이므로 건드리지 않는다.

selected.title: Set and lock a robot gripper opening stop, then verify retained motion
selected.objective: On an unpressurized, already-assembled representative SCHUNK DRG 80 bench fixture, adjust the opening-stop screw to a declared 90° total opening, lock it without changing the setting, withdraw both tools, and operate a cold test lever to verify retained opening over repeated cycles.
skills: open-ended wrench seating on a thin jam nut
coupled screw adjustment and nut locking
selected.success_conditions: Initial score is 0. Award 0.25 for a released opening within 6° of the declared 90° target; 0.5 when within 3° with nut 73 seated against the cover and nut 74 retained in its modeled installed position; 0.75 when both tools are removed and one close-open cycle returns within 3°; 1.0 after three cycles each return within 3°, stop drift is at most 2°, both nuts remain retained, and tools and robot grippers remain at least 30 mm clear for one second. Revoke angle and cycle credit whenever locking, retention, or clearance prerequisites fail. A missing screw or nut, a dropped or inaccessible tool, fixture displacement, non-finite state, or a configured maximum-opening setting outside the modeled 20°–180° adjustment range, or a violation of the fixture's actual mechanical limits, scores 0. Ordinary closing below 20° during functional cycles is permitted. Equivalent safe strategies earn the same outcome score; arm identity, order, path, action count, and impulse windows are not graded. The target, tolerances, cycle count, and clearance are explicit benchmark assumptions checkable by protractor, witness marks, nut-gap inspection, and video.
selected.industrial_value: SCHUNK specifies opening-angle adjustment, locking, and pneumatic functional testing for its DRG 44–80 industrial grippers, making this direct robot-end-effector setup work within Impact on AI timelines. Its tested ability differs from generic tightening and the accepted hose-clamp task: the robot must preserve an adjustable stop against locknut reaction and then demonstrate hands-off functional retention. It also differs from PR 1540 because two concentric tools act on a coupled screw-and-nut setting rather than stabilizing a sensor body during connector assembly, and from PR 2229 because no third-body feeler gauge or cam clamp establishes the target.
selected.dexterity: One gripper must keep a driver seated in the adjustment screw while the other seats and turns a wrench on nut 73. Tightening must physically tend to disturb an unrestrained screw, requiring coordinated countertorque, angular regulation, possible wrench regrasping, clean tool withdrawal, and subsequent operation of the articulated test fixture.

selected.asset_plan: Build independently authored, full-scale representative rigid geometry, not a redistributed SCHUNK CAD model. Preserve the catalog drawing’s dimensional semantics: 100 × 71.6 × 135.5 mm are catalog X/Y/Z reference dimensions, not a claimed bounding envelope, and the page-7 drawing separately shows a 183.35 mm extent to point P. Represent the anodized-aluminum housing, steel angular jaws, native revolute jaw joints, common centric coupling, accessible adjustment screw, nut 73 as the locking nut, and retained nut 74 as the second manufacturer-specified nut; its precise spacing and role beyond installation are disclosed fixture assumptions because the manual does not explain them. Provide real hex and wrench contact geometry and a native or conservative task-local torque/friction mechanism in which tightening disturbs an unrestrained screw. The cold lever replaces pneumatic actuation only for bench verification. Target angle, hardware dimensions absent from the manual, friction, preload, and tolerances remain declared assumptions. Before demo development, validate reset, tool seating, restrained-versus-unrestrained causality, joint traces, loss cases, release clearance, and timestep sensitivity in the pinned Isaac Sim 6.1/YAM runtime.
selected.risk: Closest ability-level neighbors include PR 1540, PR 1799, PR 1865, PR 2018, PR 2167, and PR 2229. Novelty depends on retaining genuine concentric two-tool screw/nut countertorque and functional-cycle verification; an implementation with zero driver reaction or a scripted phase flag would collapse into existing stabilization or adjustment tasks. No current native gripper trial exists, so implementation feasibility and physics validation remain future gates rather than claimed evidence.

contract.objective: On an unpressurized, already-assembled representative SCHUNK DRG 80 bench fixture, set the maximum total jaw opening to 90 degrees, lock the adjustment with nut 73 without disturbing the setting, retain nut 74, withdraw both tools, and use the cold test lever for three close-open cycles that demonstrate retained adjustment.
contract.instruction: Set and lock the gripper's maximum opening at 90 degrees. Remove the tools, operate the test lever through three complete close-open cycles, and leave the gripper open with both tools racked and the work area clear.
contract.industrial_mapping: SCHUNK DRG Assembly and Operation Manual 389041 v5.00, section 5.4.1, printed page 28, directs opening-angle adjustment with the compressed-air supply off and the gripper closed, installation of nuts 73 and 74, locking using nut 73, and subsequent functional testing by actuation. The SCHUNK DRG 80 product data sheet specifies an adjustable 20–180 degree maximum opening, an anodized-aluminum housing, steel base jaws, and 100 × 71.6 × 135.5 mm reference dimensions; its drawing separately labels 183.35 mm to point P. This task tests robot-end-effector setup through coaxial driver engagement, thin-wrench seating, coupled screw and jam-nut counterholding, preservation of an adjustable motion stop, tool withdrawal, and hands-off functional verification. The 90 degree target, simultaneous counterholding mechanism, cold test lever, tolerances, and torque/friction model are disclosed benchmark assumptions rather than manufacturer-prescribed calibration or choreography.

damage_rules: At reset define immutable disjoint primary body sets: F={fixture frame and cover}; B={bench}; M={left jaw,right jaw,piston/linkage,adjusting screw S,locking nut N73,retained nut N74,cold lever}; T={hex driver D,open wrench W}; R={all robot rigid links and fingers}; Q={rack cradles}; C={camera and mast}. G is the subset of R containing both end-effector gripper housings and all finger bodies, excluding arm bases. fixture_work=F union M. B_dyn is exactly the dynamic native bodies/articulation links in M union T union R; frame F is tested separately for mount stability. Export immutable native IDs for these sets. Membership never changes within an episode. F is dynamic, attached to B by a native fixed joint with declared finite breakForce150N and breakTorque15N*m (benchmark weak-mount assumptions). It is not a static/kinematic body or restored by the scorer. B, Q and C may be static. The standard YAM base mounting is unchanged. All dimensions, datums, material choices, fixture/tool reset poses and mount-probe parameters are specified normatively in input/fixture-geometry-contract.json and its SHA256-pinned first-party geometry manifests. No proprietary CAD or hardware calibration is claimed.

Intended unordered contact pairs I are D/socket faces of S, W/designated N73 flats, robot fingers/designated tool handles, robot fingers/cold-lever handle, jaw/stop, authored internal linkage or guide mates, tools/designated cradles or bench support, and fixture/bench mount/support. X is exactly the standard fixed robot-base/bench mounting interface; X is excluded from task damage-contact grading as permanent infrastructure, with native collision settings unchanged. Every remaining pair involving F,B,M,T,R,Q,C is N. I,N,X and all native body IDs are frozen at reset; manifold splitting does not alter classification. No essential tool/hardware or moving-robot/task contact is in X.

After every native physics integration and contact-resolution substep k, the POST_PHYSICS_STEP callback must refresh joint coordinates, body poses and velocities, actuator generalized force, and every reported point c in each pair manifold P_ab,k before any latch, cycle, dwell or score update. For point c, n_c,k is the unit normal directed from canonical lower-ID body a to higher-ID body b, J_c,k is the resolved impulse vector in N·s applied to b, s_c,k is signed separation in metres with positive meaning gap and negative meaning penetration, and u_c,k=(v_b,c,k−v_a,c,k)·n_c,k in m/s uses point velocities including angular motion.

For every manifold point define compressive impulse j_c,k=max(0,J_c,k·n_c,k) in N·s, positive penetration p_c,k=max(0,−s_c,k) in metres, and positive closing-work increment e_c,k=(j_c,k/dt_phys)·max(0,−u_c,k)·dt_phys in joules. For pair ab at substep k define j_ab,k=Σ over current P_ab,k of j_c,k, f_ab,k=j_ab,k/dt_phys in newtons, e_ab,k=Σ e_c,k, and p_ab,k=max over current P_ab,k of p_c,k, with all four equal to zero for an empty manifold. Force limits apply to f_ab,k, penetration limits to p_ab,k, and work accumulates e_ab,k. Points may be added, removed or reordered without identity tracking; only the immutable body pair owns event state, preventing manifold splitting from evading limits.

For each immutable pair, event work E_ab starts at zero on reset. A pair contact event is a maximal substep sequence with j_ab,k>0, permitting one intervening zero-impulse substep. While active, update E_ab←E_ab+e_ab,k, including zero for the permitted gap. After two consecutive substeps with j_ab,k=0, reset E_ab and the pair event state before processing any later contact. Episode hard-failure latches never reset before environment reset.

Hard failure H starts false and permanently latches on any non-finite required body, contact or joint state; broken or detached required joint; S, N73 or N74 leaving its guide or retainer by more than 3 mm; configured maximum opening outside 20–180 degrees; jaw travel more than 1 degree beyond authored mechanical limits; fixture datum translation over 10 mm or tilt over 5 degrees; or any tool-drop, tool-loss, energized-adjustment, retention, penetration, force or work violation. H immediately makes current and terminal score zero. Physics remains active: the scorer must not restore, clamp, delete or collision-disable the damaged state.

The energized-adjustment hazard is independent of tool identity and contact. Let Fact,k be absolute piston-joint generalized force in newtons; qS,k and q73,k be fresh unwrapped rotations in radians; and zS,k be fresh screw axial position in millimetres along its authored guide axis. If Fact,k>1 N and any of |qS,k−qS,k−1|/dt_phys>0.01 rad/s, |q73,k−q73,k−1|/dt_phys>0.01 rad/s, or |zS,k−zS,k−1|/dt_phys>0.01 mm/s, H latches. The force and motion thresholds are conservative benchmark assumptions. The first post-reset sample initializes previous values and cannot alone trigger this predicate.

For N pairs, H latches if p_ab,k>2 mm, f_ab,k>150 N at any physics substep, or E_ab>5 J in one pair event. For I pairs the respective limits are 2 mm, 250 N and 8 J. These conservative simulation limits are benchmark assumptions requiring independent 480 Hz refinement. Contacts, excessive forces and physical breakage remain possible and are failed by observation rather than prevented.

A tool drop occurs when D or W is neither held by simultaneous opposing robot-finger contacts nor wholly inside its designated rack cradle, its centroid falls at least 50 mm below the most recent centroid height at which it was supported by a gripper or cradle, and it subsequently reports contact impulse with F, M, Q or C. A tool is lost immediately if its centroid is more than 50 mm below the tabletop plane, outside the tabletop footprint expanded horizontally by 50 mm, or inside an enclosed fixture region while the complete designated grasp handle lacks a collision-free straight extraction cylinder 35 mm in diameter to outside that region. Either predicate latches H. A tool wholly within its designated rack cradle is supported and is not dropped.

N74 retention requires center displacement from its installed guide pose at most 2 mm and axial guide engagement at least 3 mm. N73 retention requires axial guide engagement at least 3 mm. Guide engagement is the axial overlap length between the authored nut-bore interval and guide-cylinder interval projected on their common guide axis. Rotation about that axis alone does not violate retention. Loss of either nut latches H.

No rule disables essential collisions, writes an object pose or velocity after initialization, welds a grasp, teleports a task object, grades arm identity, prescribes action order, or uses an arbitrary action or impulse window. Scripted experts may read poses, joint states, contacts and latch flags to plan normal guarded 14D joint actions but may not edit simulation state.

Ramp external world+X force0to200N linearly over1s at fixture-local(0,0,0.10)m, then hold up to2s or until native mount break plus datum translation>10mm. No pose/velocity writes. This is a physical native failure diagnostic, never a robot-success demonstration. T_F0 and the exact fixture_frame datum are defined in input/fixture-geometry-contract.json.

F_act always means the native applied powered actuator effort along the piston DOF in N, excluding gravity, passive joint reactions and clamping contact forces. Vent sets powered force capability to zero; a command/state label alone is not a measured actuator force. Native probes must verify the selected effort channel and units before grading energized motion or the vented preload window.
assets: Independently authored full-scale rigid compound representative DRG 80 fixture with anodized-aluminum frame and cover, steel angular jaws, piston/linkage, and native revolute/prismatic joints
Native guided adjustment screw S, thin locking nut N73, and separately retained nut N74 with explicit collision geometry
Hex driver D with socket-engaging tip and graspable handle
Open-ended wrench W sized for N73 with physical jaw-face contact geometry
Cold articulated test lever and finite-force actuator linkage; no pneumatic supply is represented
Rigid workbench, marked three-dimensional tool rack, camera mast and colliders, and standard bimanual YAM embodiment
Task-local independently authored source geometry and materials; manufacturer PDFs and proprietary CAD are evidence only and are not redistributed

Normative geometry/material/layout/reference datum: input/fixture-geometry-contract.json, plus referenced SHA256-pinned first-party assets/geometry.json and fixture/fixture-proposal.json; all absent manufacturer values are explicit benchmark assumptions.

Material precedence and complete helical constitutive law are normative in input/fixture-geometry-contract.json; prototype material labels are visual placeholders, not conflicting physics assignments.

Normative geometry/material/thread manifest raw file SHA256: 807d43b90b315c82d3ffbf0b5cd45373417d84f0ab504394c49e56bff63f7cd3 for input/fixture-geometry-contract.json. This is the SHA256 of exact UTF8 FILE BYTES, including formatting; it is not the canonical parsed-object digest.
approximations: The 90 degree target, ±6 and ±3 degree bands, 2 degree drift allowance, three-cycle test, 1 second clearance dwell, 30 mm clearance, hardware dimensions absent from the sources, 1.0 mm/revolution thread lead, torque, friction, force/work limits, motion thresholds and all damage thresholds are explicit benchmark assumptions rather than manufacturer calibration or safety ratings.
The manufacturer’s 20–180 degree value is the adjustable maximum total opening. Ordinary functional cycles may close below 20 degrees and are not failures.
Catalog values 100 × 71.6 × 135.5 mm are reference dimensions rather than a complete moving envelope; the separately labeled 183.35 mm extent to point P is preserved in the authored layout.
Nut 74 is present and retained, but its precise spacing and function beyond manufacturer-specified installation are modeling assumptions because the cited procedure does not explain them.

A cold finite-force lever substitutes for compressed-air functional testing. It must move the actual piston/jaw mechanism and encounter the physical stop; scorer flags or goal-driven motion cannot produce a cycle.

The assumed right-handed screw uses a 1.0 mm/revolution helical coupling. N73 tightening must transmit reaction to S. The zero-counterhold control is deliberately continued until measured setting drift exceeds 6 degrees, while the physically restrained control must stay within 2 degrees. This torque law is benchmark physics, not a claimed manufacturer procedure.

For the torque-ratio check, integrate |tauS| and |tau73| over the maximal contiguous interval in which N73 is tightening, W contacts N73 and S has no driver or robot contact. The ratio is ∫|tauS|dt/∫|tau73|dt. The test is invalid rather than passed if the denominator is below 0.05 N·m·s. Wrench seating error is the maximum distance from each active wrench jaw face to its corresponding N73 flat during that interval.

The trusted evaluator source independently sets control_hz=20. At pinned YAM commit 0059d02a1a91bc6834c1d0846022891df0c78730, scene constants set PHYSICS_DT=1/240 s and env_cfg_callback separately computes decimation from the supplied control rate; for 20 Hz this is 12 and step_dt must be 0.05 s. Native startup must assert control_hz=20, sim.dt=1/240 s, decimation=12, render_interval=12 and step_dt=0.05 s. Control timing is not inferred from observed substep count.

Refinement uses task-local sim.dt=1/480 s, decimation=24 and render_interval=24 while independently retaining the trusted 20 Hz control rate, identical initial state, commands, solver settings, materials and scoring definitions. It is a new native run, not trace resampling.

The restored input/runtime-api-preflight.json hash-verifies the pinned PhysxManager source and confirms PRE_PHYSICS_STEP and POST_PHYSICS_STEP subscriptions receive dt. It is source inspection only. Certification remains blocked until native probes verify callback order, exactly 12 or 24 fresh post-step samples per control action, reset subscription cleanup, contact-manifold point impulses and normals, point velocities, unwrapped joint coordinates, actuator generalized force/torque freshness, and units/signs.

Reset stability metrics use maxima over their stated fresh post-settle windows. Camera checks use the minimum across ten consecutive reset frames and ten final frames. Fixture pixel fraction is the number of pixels carrying immutable fixture segmentation IDs divided by 224². A missing segmentation buffer, malformed frame or zero fixture pixels fails rather than being ignored.

Refinement force difference is |P480−P240|/max(P240,1 N), where each P is the maximum manifold-summed pair force f_ab,k over the identical immutable pair set and corresponding action interval. Final-angle difference uses the final settled physical jaw angle. Contact events, work accumulators, previous axial/rotation samples, dwell counters, extrema, certificates and latches reset independently for each run.
No native component pass, YAM demonstration or successful episode is claimed by this contract. All physics observables and rates require construction-stage native validation before demo development.

Operator draft repair before contract acceptance: clearance uses grippers/tools versus the actual fixture work area, excluding permanent bases/bench; endpoints and cycles require externally released native lever/piston/stop actuation; force/work limits and all27 existing physics-check thresholds remain unchanged. The finite mount and endpoint force/speed thresholds are explicit benchmark assumptions, not manufacturer ratings. No native pass is claimed.

Locking is physical native elastic clamp preload, not a seat flag. A released vented2N minimum establishes P, which is then retained only while native clamp force and hardware prerequisites persist. The force law/compliance must physically support that preload and pass all native reaction/refinement gates. New preload criterion strengthens the unchanged27 original physics checks. Geometry and reference transforms are normative in input/fixture-geometry-contract.json. Actual observed gripper joint7/8 thresholds use pinned YAM constants, not commands. All scoring durations scale with actual physics dt.

The geometry manifest now freezes KS=1e6,KN=1e5N/m; DS=4000,DN=2500N*s/m; right-handed1mm/revolution screw/frame and N73/S helices; explicit dissipative thread friction; and lubricated N73/cover bearing mu0.08/0.05. No independent axial guide friction, contact interference, lock flag, or target servo can substitute for elastic threaded clamp preload. These are benchmark assumptions to validate natively, not SCHUNK calibration values. Anodized-aluminum frame/cover overrides generic Steel visual labels in CPU seed manifests. Bench, camera, mast and rack materials are defined. Physical constitutive parameter changes require a reviewed contract revision before certification.
contract.scoring_spec:
All measurements and state updates follow fresh POST_PHYSICS_STEP sampling and damage update. alpha is total physical jaw angle in degrees, thetaS/theta73 are unwrapped native rotations in degrees, zS is screw guide position in millimetres, and g73 is the signed N73-seat axial gap in millimetres, positive for separation. seat73 means -0.10<=g73<=0.50; negative gaps outside that tight interval cannot earn locking credit even before the independent2mm damage limit. Nut retention uses the damage-rule guide predicates. Define A=F union M, J={both jaws,piston/linkage,S,N73,N74}, U=R union T. The cold lever is in M but not J: robot contact with its handle is legitimate actuation. R_move is exactly R minus the two fixed base links; for pinned YAM it includes link1 through link5, gripper, tip_left and tip_right of each arm. Both grippers are open only if each native measured joint7 and joint8 coordinate lies in[-0.04705,-0.03756]m (80percent of the pinned-0.04695m open limit); commands alone do not establish opening. clear(X,Y) is minimum signed surface separation between collision shapes. V is the coaxial adjustment cylinder of radius45mm, from10mm below the cover seat to35mm above the reset screw mouth. A tool is outside V only if every point of its collision geometry is outside V.
The lever joint coordinate is in degrees: neutral detent [-5,+5], close detent [-35,-25], open detent [+25,+35]. The piston prismatic coordinate is in metres with closed datum qP=0; closed witness means qP<=0.00060m. These are explicit benchmark geometry assumptions. Lever open/close detents respectively command finite native opening/closing force capped at10N, other angles vent the command; no jaw-angle or scoring target controls this force. The lever commands a finite-force native piston mechanism; no angle-target servo may create a stop. The native asset must implement those exact detent/closed-datum definitions. released means no native contact point between U and J, excluding only internal mechanism pairs. Preload force f73 is the sum of compressive native normal impulses for N73/cover-seat contact points divided by actual physics dt, in N. A physical preload certificate P may be created only with measured actuator force magnitude<=0.10N, no U/J contact, seat73, retained nuts, f73>=2N and |dthetaS/dt|,|dtheta73/dt|<=1degree/s for a fresh0.25s window. P is revoked immediately by H, retention loss, failed seat73, any U/J contact, or f73<2N. Thus merely touching the seat, load from an energized piston, hand support, or screw friction alone cannot establish locking. No scorer-generated force or pose may create P. A current open endpoint requires valid P and the measured lever in its open detent, positive opening actuator force>1N, piston/S stop normal contact force>=0.1N, |dalpha/dt|<=2degrees/s, |piston axial speed|<=0.005m/s, seat73, retained nuts, and released at every fresh sample of its qualification window. A release/endpoint window lasts0.25s, requiring60 samples at240Hz or120 at480Hz. No contact availability/force is inferred from score or a scripted phase flag.
P6 is a current qualified open endpoint for0.25s with |alpha-90|<=6degrees throughout. This deliberately requires physical locking/retention: angle-only with an unseated nut earns0, resolving the selected candidate's locking prerequisite. A precise lock certificate L is created at such an endpoint only when |alpha-90|<=3degrees throughout and |thetaS(end)-thetaS(start)|<=1degree. L stores thetaS_L,zS_L, endpoint angle and native sample index. L may remain cached while the mechanism closes, because maximum opening is temporarily unobservable, but is immediately revoked by H, retention loss, seat73 becoming false, any U/J contact, |thetaS-thetaS_L|>1degree, |zS-zS_L|>0.10mm, or a newly settled native open endpoint outside90+/-3degrees. Those cumulative certificate-relative changes are the exact adjustment-motion revocation predicate; numerical jitter below them does not count. Revocation clears all cycle records and clearance dwell. Every score update uses current physical prerequisites, not a historical maximum.
A cycle starts only after L exists, when the native lever is in close detent, fresh alpha crosses downward through10degrees, and fresh piston displacement qP[k]-qP[k-1]<-1e-7m. It must reach qP<=0.00060m before reopening. Open reversal requires lever open detent and qP[k]-qP[k-1]>1e-7m. Kinematic centric coupling is checked at every substep: with qP in metres, |alpha-(3degrees+(180/pi)*300*qP)|<=1degree. The3degree closed offset is1.5degrees per jaw; the300rad/m total ratio is an explicit representative internal linkage assumption. Violation invalidates the cycle. These signed displacement and coupling predicates, finite native force, stop contact and absence of U/J contact define actuation causality; a scripted cycle flag is insufficient. It remains eligible only while L stays valid, U/J has no contact, and the stated signed-displacement/centric-coupling predicates remain satisfied; only the sign needed for the current stroke is required during motion, while zero displacement at closed/open settling is permitted. It completes after the lever enters open detent, piston meets the numeric open-reversal predicate and then reaches native stop contact, alpha crosses upward through80degrees, and a released open endpoint with |alpha-90|<=3degrees qualifies for0.25s. A cycle is the maximal close/open interval; intermediate reversals or threshold oscillations do not add cycles. ai is its final endpoint angle and L is refreshed from that endpoint. Direct robot/tool jaw or piston driving invalidates the cycle rather than counting as function testing. No robot/tool may hold the jaws or adjustment hardware to supply an endpoint. Contact is not suppressed. Define endpoint range only over completed still-valid cycle endpoints {a1,...,an}; it is0 for zero/one endpoint. Clear cycle records on L revocation or endpoint range>2degrees. C1 requires one cycle; C3 requires at least three distinct valid cycles, each endpoint90+/-3degrees and max(ai)-min(ai)<=2degrees.
CLEAR requires C3 and valid L, both tools wholly inside their designated cradles, clear(R_move union T,A)>=30mm, both grippers open, released, and a current physically stopped open endpoint within90+/-3degrees and settled as above for1.00s continuously. This requires240 fresh samples at240Hz or480 at480Hz. Permanent bases/table support are not clearance targets. Any failure resets dwell immediately. Forearm/body contact with J fails released even if grippers are clear. E25=P6; E50=valid L; E75=L and C1 and both tools outside V; E100=L and C3 and CLEAR. At each20Hz grading instant score is0 if H, otherwise max(0,0.25*E25,0.50*E50,0.75*E75,1.00*E100). Wrong final open angle, loss of release or seating revokes the associated current credit; closing alone does not revoke the cached certificate. Partial credit is precision/verification progress on a physically secured setting.
Reset clears P,H, pair-event work/state, previous motion samples, all dwells/extrema, L and cycles. Initial untouched settled score is exactly0. Action4800 finishes its native substeps and then returns the current terminal score, never a prior maximum. Early termination uses the same rule. After termination no physics, dwell, certificate, cycle or score advancement occurs. Control rate stays20Hz; every time window is measured in seconds using actual physics dt, including refinement. Equivalent safe adjustment strategies get the same outcome; no hand identity, path, arbitrary action count or preferred counterholding choreography is scored.

required_controls.name: control_untouched_initial_noop
required_controls.reason: The untouched settled maximum opening remains more than 6 degrees from 90 degrees with no inherited dwell, certificate or cycle history.

required_controls.name: control_angle_only_released_within_six
required_controls.reason: First establish valid P from native released vented N73 preload>=2N for0.25s; retain P. A subsequent released94degree stopped endpoint is within6 but outside3, so P6 earns0.25 and no precise L exists.

required_controls.name: control_locked_within_three_no_cycle
required_controls.reason: A fresh released lock certificate exists within 3 degrees, but no physical cycle has completed.

required_controls.name: control_locked_one_cycle_tools_withdrawn
required_controls.reason: One retained cycle and both tools outside the adjustment volume qualify, but three cycles and final clearance dwell are absent.

required_controls.name: control_full_three_cycle_clear_dwell
required_controls.reason: The locked setting survives three valid cycles and the racked tools and open robot grippers remain clear for one fresh second.

required_controls.name: control_wrong_angle_locked
required_controls.reason: A safely locked 105 degree setting lies outside both grading bands.

required_controls.name: control_wrong_nut_seating
required_controls.reason: A2mm N73 seat gap fails the tight seat73 interval, so neither angle/locking nor functional credit is eligible, regardless of target angle.

required_controls.name: control_unrestrained_locking_reaction
required_controls.reason: Starting from 90 degrees, zero-counterhold tightening continues until measured absolute setting drift is at least 6.01 degrees, leaving the released terminal angle outside the inclusive 6 degree band without invoking damage.

required_controls.name: control_postcycle_retention_drift
required_controls.reason: After a valid cycle, actual adjustment and resecuring with actuator vented physically establish a new valid released preload certificate P>=2N for0.25s. The new released94degree stopped endpoint is low precision. Retouch/setting change revoked old L and cycles; only P6/0.25 is eligible. Four degrees is jaw error, not screw angle.

required_controls.name: control_nut74_removed
required_controls.reason: N74 retention loss latches hard failure regardless of angle or prior progress.

required_controls.name: control_tool_drop_to_table
required_controls.reason: A qualifying unsupported 50 mm fall followed by impact latches deterministic tool-drop failure.

required_controls.name: control_fixture_displacement
required_controls.reason: A native applied load breaks the finite150N/15N*m fixture mount and translates the dynamic fixture over10mm. Broken required joint/fixture displacement gives0; no after-init state writes.

required_controls.name: control_energized_adjustment
required_controls.reason: Measured S or N73 motion above its explicit rate threshold while actuator force exceeds 1 N latches failure regardless of manipulating body or contact state.

required_controls.name: control_refinement_full_outcome
required_controls.reason: The independently executed safe full trajectory at 480 Hz must retain final score 1 and satisfy the declared angle and pair-force convergence checks.

comparisons.objective: Sets a proximity-sensor gap with a feeler leaf and secures it with a cam clamp; the candidate sets a gripper opening stop and locks a threaded adjuster.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2229 requires positioning a sensor against a third-body gauge and closing a lever; the candidate requires simultaneous coaxial driver/wrench seating and countertorque so a jam nut does not rotate the screw.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2229 checks a 1.00±0.25 mm gap, gauge removal/return, closed lever, and hands-off stability; the candidate checks a retained 90° opening after three released cycles, nut retention, drift, and clearance.
comparisons.reason: Both set and retain an adjustment, but the candidate uniquely tests coupled screw–jam-nut counterholding and post-lock articulated cycling rather than gauge-mediated placement and cam clamping.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts a gripper opening stop, locks its setting, and verifies retained motion; PR-2018 installs a two-sided door lever set while keeping it level as two screws are driven.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both involve bimanual stabilization during fastening, but the candidate requires simultaneous driver-and-wrench differential countertorque on a coupled screw/jam nut; PR-2018 supports an external lever orientation while sequentially driving mounting screws after spindle/post insertion.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a released 90° setting, seated retained nuts, ≤2° drift over three cycles, tool withdrawal, and clearance dwell; PR-2018 requires inserted and seated lever halves, snug screws, and ≤1° level alignment after release.
comparisons.reason: The shared counterholding primitive does not erase the different tested mechanism: preserving a threaded stop setpoint against concentric locknut reaction and proving cyclic retention versus holding a door lever level while mounting it. Both records provide concrete numeric success and failure criteria; no material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets a DRG 80 gripper’s opening-stop screw to 90°, locks the setting, removes the tools, and verifies retained opening through repeated actuation. PR-216 instead captures an external reference angle with a bevel gauge, carries it to a board, and transfers it by drawing a guided line.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests coaxial driver and thin-wrench seating, coupled screw/jam-nut adjustment, and bimanual countertorque that prevents locknut tightening from disturbing the stop. PR-216 explicitly has no locking screw: it fits a passive-friction hinged blade to two faces, releases the blade gripper, transports the gauge without changing its angle, seats it, and guides a marker.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate rewards target opening accuracy, seated/retained nuts, hands-off repeat-cycle return, limited stop drift, tool withdrawal, and clearance, with loss revocation. PR-216 rewards fixture fit, visible release and retained angle during carry, board seating, then line coverage, tick proximity, straightness, gap/width limits, absence of stray marks, and nib clearance. All seven available spec versions provide numeric rubric details; none are materially missing for this comparison.
comparisons.reason: Both involve adjusting and retaining an angle, but PR-216 relies on passive hinge friction to transfer a measured angle into a drawn mark, whereas the candidate tests active preservation of a screw setting against jam-nut reaction followed by functional cycling; these are meaningfully different mechanisms, manipulation abilities, and outcomes.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks a gripper opening stop before repeated actuation; PR-1501 seats a click-type torque wrench on a busbar-lug bolt and tightens only to its calibrated click.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate coordinates a hex driver and open-ended wrench to oppose locknut reaction without moving an adjustment; PR-1501 requires socket seating and force termination at a one-shot break-over cue without under- or over-torquing.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades retained opening angle, nut seating, three-cycle drift, release, and tool clearance; PR-1501 grades full socket seating, click occurrence, 90–110% peak torque, absence of unseated turning/back-off, and released stillness.
comparisons.reason: PR-1501 tests calibrated torque-cue response on one fastener, whereas the candidate tests preservation and functional retention of an adjustable setpoint while locking a coupled screw/nut pair. All versions specify numeric thresholds; no material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Adjusts a cabinet hinge side cam for even reveals and closes the flap for inspection; the candidate sets and locks a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1865 uses a slotted driver on one of several cam heads and then articulates the door; the candidate coordinates two concentric tools against locknut reaction.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1865 checks closed reveal equality, flushness, no sag, and released stability; the candidate checks nut seating, 90° opening retention, drift, and three cycles.
comparisons.reason: Both adjust and functionally inspect an articulated mechanism, but PR-1865 has no separate locking operation whose torque can disturb the chosen setting.

comparisons.objective: Assemble a loose rack into a rack-and-pinion gripper at the correct tooth phase so both fingers open symmetrically; the candidate instead adjusts and locks an already-assembled gripper's opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1898 tests rack pickup, planar alignment, gear-tooth meshing, and symmetric jaw motion. The candidate tests coaxial driver seating, thin-jam-nut wrenching, and countertorque that preserves a screw setting.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1898 requires both racks seated, each jaw opened at least 15 mm, center error within 3 mm, and hands released for 1 s. The candidate requires a retained 90° opening within 3°, three repeat cycles, no more than 2° drift, retained nuts, and 30 mm clearance. No material rubric details are missing.
comparisons.reason: Although both concern gripper mechanisms and verify motion after manipulation, gear-phase assembly is meaningfully different from preserving an adjustable stop while locking a concentric jam nut against reaction torque.

comparisons.objective: Connects an M12 sensor cable while preventing a loose sensor barrel from rotating; the candidate adjusts a stop screw and locks it with its jam nut.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1540 directly holds a large sensor body while turning a coupling ring; the candidate must keep a driver seated in the screw while a second tool turns a concentric thin nut against it.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1540 succeeds when the connector is threaded tight, the cap is stored, and hands withdraw; the candidate additionally requires a retained angular setpoint and three released functional cycles.
comparisons.reason: The close shared feature is bimanual reaction-torque control, but connector assembly against a stabilized body does not test coupled screw–nut setpoint preservation.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets a gripper’s angular stop, locks the concentric screw/jam-nut setting, then verifies repeated gripper motion. PR-2203 pulls a motor carriage against belt load, clamps it with two separate bolts, then measures belt deflection.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests simultaneous coaxial driver-and-wrench countertorque: jam-nut torque must not rotate the adjusted screw. PR-2203 tests holding a separate linear pull handle against belt restoring force while driving bolts; its complete Rig.step/Contacts.advance contains no bolt-torque-to-slide disturbance or coaxial reaction state.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires retained 90° opening, seated/retained nuts, three repeatable cycles, ≤2° drift, tool withdrawal, and 1 s clearance. PR-2203 requires 1.40–1.95 mm deflection under 2.5 N, two ≥185 N clamps, ≤0.040 mm carriage drift, belt seating/alignment, parked driver, and clear arms; its task.json does not state the check duration, though implementation uses 0.45 s.
comparisons.reason: The shared adjust-lock-release pattern is generic, but the essential causal abilities differ: resisting locking torque transferred through concentric threaded elements versus resisting pre-existing belt tension until separate clamps develop friction. PR-2203’s source does not support the prior characterization that tightening reaction disturbs its adjustment; the distinction remains conditional on the candidate actually implementing the declared screw/nut torque coupling rather than a scripted lock state.

comparisons.objective: Squares a milling vise by sweeping an indicator, adjusting yaw, securing the swivel, and verifying it; the candidate sets and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1799 requires dynamic indicator traversal, iterative alignment, and cam clamping; the candidate requires coaxial two-tool adjustment and counterholding during jam-nut tightening.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1799 checks indicator span, sweep coverage, secured yaw, and released stability; the candidate checks opening angle, lock retention, drift, and repeated actuation.
comparisons.reason: Both retain a setpoint after locking, but indicator-guided fixture alignment and cam securing are meaningfully different from countertorquing coupled threaded elements.

comparisons.objective: Adjust a drum-brake star wheel until the drum has light drag; the candidate sets a gripper opening-stop screw to 90°, locks it, and verifies retained opening.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2167 requires inserting and levering a brake spoon through a backing-plate slot, engaging successive teeth, regrasping, and turning the drum to assess drag. The candidate requires simultaneous hex-driver counterholding and thin-wrench tightening on a coupled screw and nut.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2167 succeeds at 22–28 star-wheel clicks with light drag, spoon deposited, and hands clear for 1 s; overadjustment to lock scores 0. The candidate requires angle tolerance, nut retention, three close-open cycles, bounded drift, and tool clearance. No material rubric details are missing; PR-2167 discloses that shoe motion and drag are approximated from click count.
comparisons.reason: Both share the generic adjust-then-functionally-check pattern, but the brake task tests blind notched levering and drag judgment, whereas the candidate's defining ability is two-tool countertorque that prevents a screw setting from moving during locknut tightening.

comparisons.objective: Pushes a hose fully onto a barb and tightens a worm-drive clamp; the candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1892 requires axial hose seating, clamp placement, socket engagement, and driver regrasping; the candidate requires simultaneous counterrotation of a screw and jam nut.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1892 checks hose depth, clamp location, snug/tight state, and released clearance; the candidate checks retained opening angle and repeated articulated operation.
comparisons.reason: Generic screw turning is insufficient overlap; hose insertion and circumferential clamping do not test preservation of a coupled adjuster setting.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts a gripper stop screw, locks its concentric jam nut without shifting the setting, then cycles the gripper; PR-236 supports a gravity-loaded inspection arm at an angle and engages a separate indexed clamp knob.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires simultaneous hex-driver and thin-wrench seating with countertorque against screw rotation caused by tightening its concentric nut; PR-236 instead supports an arm against gravity while turning a spatially separate knob whose reduced-order model supplies no lock reaction to the knob.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a locked 90° setting retained within 3°, ≤2° drift over three released cycles, retained nuts, and 30 mm tool clearance; PR-236 requires the +15° arm aim, indexed lock engagement, and a two-second released hold within 3°/2° drift.
comparisons.reason: The essential tested causality differs: preserving a threaded adjustment against concentric locknut reaction is not subsumed by holding a payload against gravity while actuating a separate indexed lock, although both share generic set-lock-release primitives.

comparisons.objective: Feeds a cable through a gland, tightens its cap nut, and verifies pull retention; the candidate calibrates and locks an angular stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2145 combines deformable-cable insertion with threaded cap tightening and seal compression; the candidate uses two rigid tools to counterhold a screw during jam-nut locking.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2145 checks sheath depth, a bounded nut-turn window, 30 N pull retention, and crushing; the candidate checks angular accuracy, drift, nut retention, cycling, and clearance.
comparisons.reason: Both tighten threaded hardware and perform a retention test, but cable sealing/pull anchorage does not measure coupled setpoint preservation under locknut torque.

comparisons.objective: Seals a carton seam and end tabs with a tape gun; the candidate adjusts and locks robot gripper hardware.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1893 requires tape-gun control, flap restraint, adhesive placement, tearing, and smoothing; the candidate requires precision two-tool threaded adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1893 checks seam coverage, alignment, torn tape, bonded tabs, flat flaps, and release; the candidate checks locked angular motion and repeated cycles.
comparisons.reason: The objectives, mechanisms, manipulation skills, and observable outcomes are unrelated.

comparisons.objective: Calibrates a torque-limiting clutch so it carries a light proof load and slips on a heavy one; the candidate sets a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1110 requires preload adjustment, selector operation, crank testing, and interpreting two load responses; the candidate requires jam-nut countertorque with coaxial tools.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1110 requires both proof tests at one unchanged preload and released stability; the candidate requires a retained 90° mechanical stop over three cycles.
comparisons.reason: PR-1110 tests load-dependent clutch calibration, not locking an angular adjuster while resisting tightening reaction.

comparisons.objective: Calibrates gripper force using a spring reference and zero/span/verify controls; the candidate mechanically adjusts a gripper's opening limit.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1645 requires controlled pad compression and ordered button operation while holding a reference load; the candidate requires two-tool threaded counterholding.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1645 checks zeroing, 8.5–10.5 mm spring compression, span capture, and unloaded verification; the candidate checks angular-stop locking and repeated motion retention.
comparisons.reason: Shared gripper context does not create overlap: force-sensor calibration and mechanical opening-stop locking test different abilities and outcomes.

comparisons.objective: Moves two backlash-affected sliders to target readings and locks each dial; the candidate sets one gripper stop and secures it mechanically.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-779 requires reversal-aware compensation of display hysteresis and button presses; the candidate requires physical driver/wrench engagement and opposing torque on coupled threads.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-779 checks both displayed setpoints within ±2.5 mm and latched lock buttons; the candidate checks a locked 90° opening, ≤2° drift, and three actuation cycles.
comparisons.reason: Both contain setpoints and locking, but software-display backlash compensation with pushbutton latching does not test mechanical jam-nut countertorque or functional stop retention.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks a robot-gripper opening stop; PR-2209 seals a preloaded carton by peeling, paying out, applying, wrapping, and cutting tape from an ordinary loose roll.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests rigid two-tool screw-and-jam-nut countertorque plus articulated verification; PR-2209 tests flush tape-edge acquisition, flexible-material payout, pressure adhesion, end wrapping, and blade cutting.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades retained angular adjustment and repeated motion after tool withdrawal; PR-2209 grades connected tape coverage across 44 seam cells, two 35 mm end wraps, blade severing, detachment, and a two-second released seal.
comparisons.reason: Flexible tape sourcing, adhesion, wrapping, and cutting test a materially different ability from maintaining a threaded stop setting during locknut tightening; PR-2209 lacks a formal task.json, full demonstration, model run, media, and validated complete-task allowance, but those omissions do not create plausible overlap.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a robot-gripper opening stop; PR-2208 turns over an upright taped carton, cuts three bottom-tape paths, opens four bottom flaps, and collapses the intact carton flat.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests coaxial tool seating and coupled screw/nut countertorque; PR-2208 tests whole-carton turnover, guarded-blade path tracking, outward flap articulation, and intact wall-tube collapse.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a retained 90° opening through three cycles with nuts retained and tools clear; PR-2208 requires measured turnover, all 158 cut cells, four flaps opened at least 150°, then all board vertices within a 24 mm slab for a one-second released hold.
comparisons.reason: Carton turnover, cutting, flap opening, and flattening do not exercise the candidate's coupled adjustment-preservation mechanism; PR-2208 lacks a formal task.json, complete-task run limit, full demo, model run, and media, but its tested outcome is still clearly unrelated.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and mechanically locks a robot-gripper opening stop; PR-2207 operates a handheld dryer and manipulates articulated hair to dry exposed and occluded regions while the mannequin head remains fixed.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests rigid driver/wrench counterholding and functional cycling; PR-2207 tests switch operation, dryer pickup and aiming, deformable lock separation, airflow exposure, and thermal control.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires angular accuracy, nut retention, three repeatable cycles, limited drift, and released clearance; PR-2207 requires at least 90% water removal on every hair patch, temperature at most 50°C, fixed-head integrity, power off, parking, and a one-second released hold.
comparisons.reason: Deformable hair exposure and geometry-dependent drying are meaningfully different from threaded stop adjustment and jam-nut locking; PR-2207 lacks a formal task.json, demonstrated full-task allowance, full demo, model run, and media, without making the novelty distinction ambiguous.

comparisons.objective: PR-1784 safely isolates and depressurizes a pneumatic manifold, removes a tube from a push-to-connect fitting, inserts a blanking plug, and verifies retention; the candidate sets and locks a gripper opening stop and verifies retained motion.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1784 requires lockout, dump verification, collet depression while extracting a flexible tube, plug insertion, and a pull test; the candidate requires concentric driver-and-wrench seating, bimanual countertorque that preserves a screw setting, tool withdrawal, and articulated cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1784 grades safe release history, tube removal, plug seating/grip, a 15 N retention test, and clearance; the candidate grades 90° adjustment accuracy, jam-nut locking, three repeatable cycles, limited drift, hardware retention, and released clearance.
comparisons.reason: The tested abilities and outcomes are meaningfully different despite both involving industrial hardware and hands-off retention; no material PR-1784 rubric detail is missing, while the candidate discloses that nut 74's precise role is unspecified.

comparisons.objective: Draft task unlatches an Ethernet plug in a crowded panel and transfers it to another port; the candidate sets and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2210 requires small spring-tab depression, constrained plug withdrawal/insertion, flexible-cable management, and avoiding neighboring plugs; the candidate requires two-tool threaded counterholding.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2210 proposes source release before withdrawal, target seating and latch re-engagement, neighbor retention, and a released hold; the candidate checks angular-stop retention and cycling.
comparisons.reason: Connector unlatching and insertion in cable clutter are mechanically and observably different from screw–jam-nut calibration.

comparisons.objective: Thread and tighten a spin-on oil filter to gasket contact and then to a prescribed turn or 18 N·m; the candidate adjusts and locks a gripper opening stop before cycling it.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1405 tests grasping and rotating a large threaded can, with later versions seating a cap wrench and applying ratchet torque. The candidate tests fine coaxial driver engagement plus a separate open-ended wrench on a thin nut while counterholding the adjustment screw.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1405 grades final rotation past gasket contact, penalizes loose, removed, or overcrushed filters, and requires release and wrench removal in later versions. The candidate grades retained 90° opening, nut retention, three motion cycles, drift, and clearance. No material rubric details are missing across the recorded versions.
comparisons.reason: Threaded tightening and tool release are shared primitives, but PR-1405 does not test preserving an independently adjustable stop against locknut reaction or validating that setting through repeated articulated cycles.

comparisons.objective: PR-1570 closes an adjustable wrench snugly on a nylon nut, loosens the nut in the safe direction, and sets the wrench down; the candidate sets and locks an opening-stop screw on a gripper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1570 tests thumbwheel adjustment, jaw-clearance control, correct fixed-jaw loading, breakaway pulling, and tool removal; the candidate tests coaxial driver seating plus simultaneous wrench seating and countertorque to prevent setting drift.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1570 grades loosened angle, loose-jaw and wrong-direction faults, wrench set-down, and release; the candidate grades angular accuracy, jam-nut seating, repeated retained motion, stop drift, hardware retention, and clearance.
comparisons.reason: The shared wrench-and-nut primitive is insufficient for overlap because PR-1570 tests adjustable-wrench fit and pull direction, whereas the candidate tests coupled two-tool lockup without disturbing a setting; no material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Dials a three-number padlock combination and pulls the shackle open; the candidate adjusts and locks industrial gripper hardware.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2158 requires precise multi-turn dial control with reversals and regrasping on a swinging body; the candidate requires coupled two-tool countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2158 checks successive wheel-gate alignment, shackle release, remaining on the hasp, and released stillness; the candidate checks locked opening angle and repeated cycles.
comparisons.reason: Rotary precision is the only generic commonality; the mechanisms, required coordination, and success outcomes differ materially.

comparisons.objective: PR-771 closes an edge joint between two boards by pumping a one-hand bar clamp and leaves sustained clamping force; the candidate adjusts and locks a robot-gripper opening stop and verifies its motion.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-771 tests placing a clamp around boards, repeated trigger strokes, board alignment, and force buildup; the candidate tests precision screw adjustment, thin-nut wrenching, bimanual counterholding, tool withdrawal, and lever-driven cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-771 grades jaw and joint gaps, at least 20 N clamping force, board alignment, release, stillness, and loss from the table; the candidate grades a 90° setting, lock retention, three repeatable cycles, drift, retained nuts, and clearance.
comparisons.reason: The tasks share only generic force application and hands-off verification, not the same mechanism, manipulation, or outcome; no material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks a gripper opening stop and verifies retained articulation; pr-1690 mounts a bicycle tire bead into a rim while avoiding tube damage.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial driver/wrench counterholding so jam-nut torque does not disturb a screw setting, followed by tool withdrawal and lever-actuated cycling. pr-1690 requires bimanual bead depression into the drop center and controlled rolling of a deformable tire section over the flange.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades retained 90° opening, seated/retained nuts, repeated return accuracy, limited drift, and hands-off clearance. pr-1690 grades bead seating, valve alignment, hand clearance, partial bead-channel progress, and leak/pinch avoidance; its versions provide numeric thresholds.
comparisons.reason: The objectives, manipulated mechanisms, force-control problem, and observable outcomes test meaningfully different abilities; shared bimanual coordination is only a generic primitive.

comparisons.objective: Candidate calibrates and locks an articulated gripper stop; PR-1506 prepares a moka pot by controlling water level, inserting the coffee basket, and threading the upper chamber onto the base.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate needs two-tool coaxial countertorque and subsequent articulated verification; PR-1506 needs controlled pouring, basket placement, thread starting without cross-threading, and bimanual rotation of two vessel halves.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a released 90° opening retained through three cycles with ≤2° drift and both nuts retained; PR-1506 requires 122.5–155.8 mL water, basket/coffee present, straight gasket-compressing thread engagement, limited spill, upright release, and no cross-threading.
comparisons.reason: Although both include bimanual rotation and tightening, PR-1506 tests fluid dosing and mating two large threaded bodies, not counterholding a precision adjuster during jam-nut locking or verifying a retained motion stop. Numeric outcome and damage conditions are present across its versions.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks an angular-gripper stop while preserving its setting, then verifies retained motion; pr-890 drives a started bracket bolt to seated contact with a ratchet in confined access.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires simultaneous driver countertorque and thin-jam-nut wrenching on a coupled screw/nut setting, followed by functional cycling. pr-890 requires ratchet pickup, socket alignment, and repeated short drive/return strokes that advance one threaded fastener between walls.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades target opening accuracy, nut retention, post-lock cycle repeatability, stop drift, tool withdrawal, and clearance. The latest pr-890 spec grades axial bolt advance, actual head/bracket seating, thread integrity, and a 0.5-second seated dwell; torque and cycle counts are diagnostic, although earlier versions required six productive cycles.
comparisons.reason: Both involve tools and threaded hardware, but pr-890 tests confined ratcheting to seat a fastener, whereas the candidate tests preservation of an adjustable setpoint against locknut reaction and hands-off functional retention.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts robot-gripper hardware; this record closes a used needle's hinged safety sheath and deposits the syringe in a sharps tray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires bimanual coaxial tool engagement and countertorque; the record requires one-handed surface-assisted sheath latching while avoiding the exposed needle.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks retained opening and lock integrity; the record checks a positively latched sheath, safe clearances, tray placement, release, and no forbidden needle contact.
comparisons.reason: The record tests sharps-safe one-handed latching and disposal, with no adjustable setting or coupled screw/nut mechanics.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks a gripper opening stop; this record inserts and secures a drill bit in a keyed chuck.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate counterholds an adjustment screw with a driver while turning a thin jam nut; the record stabilizes a drill and keeps a chuck key meshed against increasing separating force.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a retained 90° stop across repeated actuation; the record requires a centered, captured bit that resists torque and pull, with the key removed.
comparisons.reason: The shared need to maintain tool engagement under torque is generic; chuck clamping does not test preserving a calibrated setting against jam-nut reaction.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts, locks, and cycle-checks a gripper opening stop; PR-1288 selects and installs the matching driver bit, power-tightens a loose drawer knob, and returns the stopped tool.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires concurrent wrench/driver seating and countertorque on coupled adjustment hardware; PR-1288 requires visual bit selection, bit insertion, powered screw engagement, drawer stabilization, and tool return.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate scores retained target angle, locknut seating, repeated-cycle drift, tool removal, and clearance; PR-1288 scores stable correct-bit installation, ≥1.3 mm powered screw feed, ≤0.2 mm knob gap, a 5 N hold test, and stable tool release in its stand.
comparisons.reason: PR-1288 tests tool configuration and powered fastening of a loose screw, while the candidate tests preserving a tunable stop against locknut reaction and demonstrating retained articulated function. Both provide complete numeric scoring and loss conditions.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and mechanically locks a robot-gripper opening limit; PR-1493 performs a dipstick inspection sequence, reads oil level, reports ADD/OK/OVER, and restores the equipment.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses coaxial tools, differential countertorque, and functional cycling; PR-1493 requires handle-only dipstick extraction/reinsertion, a measured wiping stroke, visual level classification, and puck placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a released 90° stop with retained nuts and ≤2° drift over three cycles; PR-1493 requires a ≥5.4 cm wipe, full reseat, second-pull one-second reading, correct pocket report, final reseating, and rag release, with guessing or blade handling scoring zero.
comparisons.reason: The tasks test unrelated physical abilities and outcomes: mechanical adjustment retention versus contamination-safe fluid-level inspection and reporting. PR-1493's available versions include explicit procedure, thresholds, failure cases, and final-state requirements.

comparisons.objective: Both establish a machine setting and secure it, but the candidate sets an angular opening stop while this record positions a cylinder slot sensor at its switching-band midpoint.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires simultaneous concentric driver and wrench action with countertorque against jam-nut reaction; the record drags and clamps one sensor through a single seated hex driver using LED feedback.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a locked 90° stop retained over three close-open cycles; the record requires sensor position within tolerance, clamp resistance, and correct LED switching when the cylinder moves.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest record, but it does not test the candidate's defining coupled screw/jam-nut counterholding ability; its setting is translational and feedback-located through one tool.

comparisons.objective: Candidate calibrates and locks an angular gripper stop, then verifies repeatable motion; PR-1814 releases a hot air-fryer basket from hooks or a button-operated catch and transfers it to a heat-proof mat.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires two-tool countertorque and angular setpoint preservation; PR-1814 requires maintaining a release input during lifting or sliding clear of hooks, grasping a cool handle, collision avoidance, and controlled placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades opening accuracy, seated retained nuts, three-cycle drift, tool withdrawal, and clearance dwell; PR-1814 grades release actuation, basket clearance, on-mat pose, release/stillness, and permanent-zero hot-contact, bypass, or drop faults.
comparisons.reason: PR-1814 tests keyed release and safe transport under hot-surface constraints, not coupled adjustment locking or cyclic setpoint retention. Its versions specify numeric release, placement, contact, drop, and dwell conditions; no material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets a gripper motion limit; this record releases a camera plate from a cam-clamped mount and transfers it to a pad.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses two coaxial tools to resist lock reaction; the record rotates a release cam, clears a separate rear lip, and supports a payload during removal.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate verifies retained opening after cycles; the record checks cam release, mount clearance, supported upright pad placement, release, and stability without dropping.
comparisons.reason: Cam release and retained-payload dismounting test disengagement and transfer rather than calibration, countertorque, or post-lock functional retention.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks a gripper stop; this record clamps wood in a screw vise and saws a 150 mm piece.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate performs fine coupled screw/nut countertorque; the record tightens a vise and maintains an unguided saw cut through material.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks retained angular function; the record checks prior clamping, physical separation, a 150±1 mm retained length, intact positioning, and saw clearance.
comparisons.reason: Workholding and material removal to length test forceful cutting accuracy, not an adjustable mechanism's lock retention.

comparisons.objective: Place two setting blocks at marked quarter points and install a glass unit in a window frame so it stands on both blocks without touching the sill.
comparisons.physical_skill: Precise block placement followed by constrained glass insertion, including tilted room-side insertion in later versions, alignment against a stop, controlled support and release.
comparisons.success_condition: Glass stands released and still in the rebate on both correctly placed blocks, centred and upright, with any sill contact, severe tilt or loss causing zero. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: This tests support preparation and collision-free insertion of a fragile panel into a narrow frame, not coupled screw adjustment, locknut countertorque or post-lock actuation retention.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets a gripper’s adjustable opening stop to 90°, secures it with a jam nut, and verifies retained jaw motion over repeated cycles. PR-2248 instead positions a gauge block, closes a micrometer to measurement contact using its ratchet, and locks the reading.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests simultaneous driver counterholding and wrench tightening so locknut reaction does not disturb a screw setting, followed by tool withdrawal and articulated cycling. PR-2248 tests precise block placement, ratchet-only contact with counted slip clicks, avoidance of thimble overtravel, and lock-lever actuation; it does not require concentric two-tool countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires opening-angle accuracy, seated/retained nuts, three repeat cycles with limited stop drift, and hands-off clearance. PR-2248 requires the block remain aligned between the faces, a 20.000 mm gap tolerance, at least three valid ratchet clicks, lever locking, no squeeze or fall, and hands-off stability. Missing details: candidate hardware dimensions and torque/friction parameters remain future declared assumptions, while PR-2248 explicitly does not model the ratchet torque limit; neither omission obscures the different tested outcomes.
comparisons.reason: Although both involve setting and locking an adjustable mechanism, the candidate’s defining ability is preserving a screw-set gripper stop against jam-nut reaction and proving cyclic retention, whereas PR-2248’s defining ability is controlled micrometer contact through ratchet slip and measurement locking.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts gripper travel; this record removes a cordless-drill battery and places it in a tray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate counterholds a screw during jam-nut tightening; the record simultaneously squeezes two release buttons while stabilizing the drill and sliding the pack along rails.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks angle retention after locking; the record checks remembered dual-button release, pack separation, tray placement, drill displacement, release, and stillness.
comparisons.reason: Simultaneous latch release and sliding extraction test a different bimanual mechanism and endpoint.

comparisons.objective: Sharpen both faces of a kitchen knife on a whetstone and return it safely to the chopping block.
comparisons.physical_skill: Maintain a 13–22° bevel angle and near-level blade while making edge-leading heel-to-tip abrasive strokes, reorienting for both faces and safely releasing the knife.
comparisons.success_condition: Later versions require ten qualifying strokes and coverage of at least 12 of 16 edge points per face in simulation, or measured sharpness at three of four points in reality, plus a stable edge-away put-down for full score. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Although both tasks regulate an angle, knife sharpening tests sustained abrasive contact, stroke direction and full-edge coverage rather than setting and mechanically locking an articulated stop against tightening reaction.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts robot hardware; this record rinses highlighted teeth, evacuates water, and returns dental tools.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses concentric rotary tools; the record coordinates irrigator coverage and suction placement, including timed post-rinse clearance and tool return.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks retained mechanical motion; the record checks crown wetting, water recovery, spill limits, near-dry final state, tool poses, release, and dwell.
comparisons.reason: Coordinated liquid delivery and evacuation have different manipulation, hazards, and observable outcomes from threaded adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks a gripper opening stop and verifies retained motion; PR-1300 places a nickel strip and spot-welds four battery terminals.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires concentric driver-and-wrench countertorque while preserving a screw setting; PR-1300 requires thin-strip placement and repeated dual-probe positioning.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades retained 90° opening, seated/retained nuts, three repeat cycles, drift and released clearance; PR-1300 grades strip alignment, four weld contacts/bonds, welder return and stillness. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Battery-tab placement and localized welding do not test coupled screw/jam-nut adjustment or retention of an articulated stop.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop; this record bleeds air from a brake caliper through repeated pedal-and-bleeder cycles.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate applies simultaneous countertorque at one coaxial assembly; the record coordinates a pedal with a wrench at a separate valve, enforcing close-before-release timing.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks retained opening angle after three cycles; the record scores air removed and permanently fails if pedal return draws air through an open bleeder.
comparisons.reason: Both use repeated actuation and a wrench, but brake bleeding tests hydraulic sequencing and state reduction rather than preservation of a mechanical setting.

comparisons.objective: Candidate configures a gripper stop; this record mounts a shaft between fixed and spring-loaded bench centres.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses coaxial driver/wrench countertorque; the record holds a tailstock lever retracted while seating and pivoting a shaft onto two conical points.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks locked angular travel; the record checks both centre points properly seated, lever returned, shaft still, hands clear, and no damaging ram/drop.
comparisons.reason: Lever-held precision shaft seating tests alignment and compliant insertion, not threaded setting and lock retention.

comparisons.objective: Candidate mechanically calibrates and locks a gripper stop; PR-2265 diagnoses which armoured-cable core leaks to earth.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses two concentric tools for rotational counterholding; PR-2265 simultaneously cranks a tester, seats a probe on three studs, reads the dial and selects a flag.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires locked angle retention through three cycles; PR-2265 requires all cores tested under sufficient crank speed, only the leaking core flagged, prod returned and released stillness. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Simultaneous cranking and electrical probing tests sustained diagnostic tool use, not preservation of a threaded mechanical adjustment during locknut tightening.

comparisons.objective: Align a suction tool plate with a robot quick-change flange and actuate its locking ring so the tool remains suspended; the candidate sets and locks an internal gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1054 tests carrying a tool, precise flange/dowel alignment, holding it seated, and operating a locking lever with the other hand. The candidate tests dual-tool coaxial seating and coordinated screw-versus-jam-nut countertorque, followed by operating a test lever.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1054 requires the correct tool seated and locked, the wrong tool never locked, hands clear, and arms returned; its versions specify dowel capture and ring-angle thresholds. The candidate requires a numeric opening angle, repeated retained motion, limited drift, hardware retention, and tool clearance. No material rubric details are missing.
comparisons.reason: Both involve bimanual stabilization during locking, but PR-1054 principally measures component alignment, insertion, and latch retention, while the candidate measures preservation of a calibrated rotational setting under tightening reaction and subsequent cycle stability.

comparisons.objective: Candidate configures gripper hardware; this record proves a voltage detector before and after testing a conductor and tags or withdraws appropriately on failure.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses two rotary hand tools; the record balances a long stick-mounted detector, presses tester controls, contacts target points, and reacts to indicator state.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks retained mechanical adjustment; the record checks valid pre/post proofs, correct test behavior, safe final separation, release, and stillness.
comparisons.reason: Electrical-test procedural verification and long-tool handling do not overlap the candidate's coupled adjustment mechanics.

comparisons.objective: Candidate configures robot hardware; this record removes individual gnocchi from simmering water after they float and turns off the burner.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate performs coupled rotary adjustment; the record tracks asynchronous food-state changes and uses a slotted spoon for timed retrieval without direct contact.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks retained angular motion; the record checks timely removal to a plate, burner shutdown, release/stability, and no gripper-food contact.
comparisons.reason: State-triggered utensil retrieval and heat shutdown are unrelated to threaded adjustment and countertorque.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks an angular-gripper opening stop; PR-998 loads a housing into a rollover fixture, retains and inverts it, locks the cradle, then fits a pad.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial driver seating, thin-nut wrenching and countertorque; PR-998 requires part loading, sliding-bar closure, crank rotation, lock-bolt insertion and recessed placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades target angle, nut retention, repeated actuation and drift; PR-998 grades correct housing orientation, retention before inversion, 180° fixture angle, bolt engagement, pad seating and released stillness. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Both involve locking, but PR-998 tests safe fixture sequencing and inversion rather than coupled threaded calibration preserved against tightening reaction.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets a gripper stop to a specified angle; this record fits opposed tapered shims behind a door jamb until snug without bowing it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate resists jam-nut torque with a coaxial driver; the record incrementally drives two opposed wedges, senses fit, and balances contact pressure from both wall faces.
