comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks lock retention over actuation cycles; the record checks shim overlap, near-zero free gap, bounded jamb bow, rest, and hand clearance.
comparisons.reason: Both preserve a target while securing it, but opposed-wedge fit and jamb straightness test force-balanced insertion rather than coupled threaded countertorque.

comparisons.objective: Sweep test rods through two light-curtain fields, observe which curtain fails, and tag out that machine; the candidate mechanically adjusts and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2070 tests controlled rod sweeping across complete sensing fields, maintaining orientation and speed, perceiving lamp state, and inserting a tag. The candidate tests precision driver and wrench use, countertorque, regrasping, and articulated verification.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2070 requires all 45 cells of both fields covered, correct post-test tagging, rods withdrawn, release, stillness, and no dropped rod or tag. The candidate requires retained angular accuracy over three cycles with nuts retained and tools clear. No material rubric details are missing.
comparisons.reason: Safety-field coverage and fault-dependent tagging exercise inspection and decision-guided placement, not coupled screw adjustment, jam-nut locking, or retention of a mechanical calibration.

comparisons.objective: Calibrate a fixed tool tip by touching one reference point from four sufficiently different wrist orientations; candidate instead sets and locks a gripper opening stop, then cycles it to verify retention.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-827 tests precise single-tool pivoting about a stationary contact with stable one-second holds. The candidate tests coaxial driver/wrench seating, bimanual countertorque, setting preservation during jam-nut locking, tool withdrawal, and lever actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-827 awards 0.25 per qualified contact pose, requiring four distinct axes for full score. The candidate grades released opening accuracy, installed nut retention, three repeat cycles, limited drift, and one-second tool/gripper clearance, with prerequisite revocation and loss failures.
comparisons.reason: The tasks test meaningfully different abilities: multi-orientation TCP contact calibration versus mechanically locking an adjustable stop against tightening reaction and proving hands-off retained motion.

comparisons.objective: Select and mount the undamaged grinding wheel with the complete ordered flange/blotter stack, tighten it safely, and verify secure mounting; candidate instead adjusts and locks an already-assembled gripper opening stop at a target angle.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-871 emphasizes inspection choice, repeated coaxial insertion of keyed and annular parts, spindle restraint, and torque-window tightening. The candidate emphasizes simultaneous driver-and-wrench counterholding so a screw setting does not rotate while its jam nut is locked, followed by tool withdrawal and articulation.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-871 scores ordered stack completion, nut seating below an irreversible overtorque limit, released spindle-lock/hand clearance, low slip in a braked spin, and limited axial motion under tug. The candidate scores target-angle accuracy, nut retention, three close-open returns, at most 2° drift, and sustained 30 mm clearance, with revocation on locking or retention failure.
comparisons.reason: Both include nut tightening, clearance, and post-tightening functional checks, but PR-871 tests safe ordered wheel-stack assembly and clamp adequacy, whereas the candidate's defining ability is preserving an adjustable screw setting against coupled locknut reaction.

comparisons.objective: Angle a full-size click-lock vinyl tile tongue into an installed row and lower it flat to lock.
comparisons.physical_skill: Long-edge insertion into a narrow groove while coordinating the unsupported near edge, followed by contact-driven lowering and locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Tile ends flat, aligned to the row and spacer, with its long click joint fully engaged and no raised/open seam; incomplete engagement earns only partial credit.
comparisons.reason: Its tested ability is long compliant-profile edge engagement and lowering, not torque-preserving screw adjustment, jam-nut locking, or retained cycle verification.

comparisons.objective: Candidate calibrates and locks a robot-gripper stop; PR-1941 fills and removes an evacuated blood tube while an inserted needle remains stable.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both use bimanual stabilization, but the candidate counters rotational locknut torque with concentric tools, whereas PR-1941 counterholds a needle holder during axial stopper piercing and tube extraction.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires retained opening across three cycles with bounded drift and nuts retained; PR-1941 requires fill, tube removal and tray placement while needle displacement/tilt or holder release irreversibly fails. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: The shared generic counterholding primitive serves different force axes, mechanisms and outcomes: threaded calibration retention versus atraumatic axial tube exchange.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a robot gripper’s opening stop at 90° and verifies retained actuation; PR-757 strips 8–12 mm of insulation from a cable using a lever-operated benchtop station.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial driver and thin-wrench seating, coupled screw–jam-nut countertorque, setting preservation, tool withdrawal, and articulated cycling. PR-757 requires depth-controlled cable insertion, sustained lever depression against spring/cutting force, and straight cable extraction while the blades remain closed.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate scores angular accuracy, nut retention, limited stop drift across three cycles, and one-second hands-off clearance, with loss revocation. PR-757 scores insertion progress, completed stripping length, lever release, and gripper clearance, with explicit cut/pull force checks in its latest version.
comparisons.reason: The tasks share bimanual force coordination and release verification only at a generic level; one tests preserving a precision mechanical adjustment during locknut tightening and subsequent cyclic retention, while the other tests cable positioning and material removal under a held cutting mechanism.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks a gripper opening limit; PR-1572 safely routes a curved board edge using a starting pin and bearing-guided bit.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses seated hand tools and coordinated countertorque; PR-1572 braces and pivots a free board onto a bearing, then feeds its curve in the safe direction while maintaining cutter clearance.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades angle accuracy, lock retention, cyclic return and drift; PR-1572 grades routed length, safe pin-mediated entry, feed direction, hand exclusion and final cutter clearance. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Guided curved-stock feeding around a cutting hazard does not exercise threaded stop adjustment or locknut-induced setting preservation.

comparisons.objective: Install an O-ring over a hydraulic plug thread into its groove without excessive stretch or twist.
comparisons.physical_skill: Controlled elastomer stretching, axial transfer over threads, square release, and seating correction.
comparisons.success_condition: Ring is fully seated and released in the groove, remains within the 50% stretch and 90° roll limits, and has no side left on the thread; damage limits force zero.
comparisons.reason: The record tests deformable seal handling and damage avoidance, whereas the candidate tests coupled rigid screw/nut adjustment and retained articulated function.

comparisons.objective: Candidate calibrates and locks an articulated gripper stop; PR-1694 rolls puff pastry into a uniformly thick, sufficiently long sheet.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires fine tool seating and rotational counterholding; PR-1694 requires level rolling-pin control across deformable material over repeated passes.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a retained 90° opening through three cycles; PR-1694 grades sheet length, thickness distribution/evenness, damage and released pin placement. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Deformable thickness control with a spacer-ring rolling pin is a different tested ability from coupled screw-and-jam-nut calibration.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks a gripper opening stop; PR-1992 packs fifteen pool balls tightly on the foot spot and removes the triangle without disturbance.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate applies coordinated countertorque through concentric tools; PR-1992 compresses a group of free-rolling spheres, aligns the pack and lifts a surrounding frame cleanly.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades angle tolerance, nut seating, repeated-cycle retention and drift; PR-1992 grades ball-pair gaps, spot/orientation accuracy, rack clearance and displacement-free release. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Careful hands-off retention is shared only generically; packing and releasing rolling objects does not test threaded calibration under locknut reaction.

comparisons.objective: Activate a handheld 3D scanner and cover at least 95% of a cast housing's outer surface, including its top; the candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2016 tests button actuation, scanner handling at valid standoff and view angle, turntable coordination, occlusion planning, and tracking recovery. The candidate tests coaxial hand-tool use, countertorque, wrench regrasping, and mechanical cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2016 requires 95% scan coverage, top coverage, final clearance, and no part disturbance, scanner collision, or drop. The candidate requires a retained 90° opening through three cycles with bounded drift and retained hardware. No material rubric details are missing; scanner facing and tracking limits are explicitly labeled assumptions.
comparisons.reason: Surface-view planning and noncontact inspection do not establish overlap with two-tool mechanical adjustment, locknut reaction control, or functional retention testing.

comparisons.objective: Take a tympanic temperature by seating a covered probe, pressing Measure, holding it steady through the reading, and laying it down.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fine probe-to-canal alignment, steady unsupported holding during button actuation, and controlled withdrawal.
comparisons.success_condition: A valid three-second reading is completed without unseating or exceeding 1.5 mm/3° motion, then the thermometer is released still on the table; excessive insertion or dropping forces zero.
comparisons.reason: It tests steady medical probe placement through a timed measurement, not threaded stop adjustment, countertorque locking, or cyclic retention.

comparisons.objective: Place a pepper seedling plug, backfill it evenly, firm it, and leave it upright without damage; the candidate adjusts and locks a robot gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2106 tests delicate plug handling, granular backfilling around a held object, support formation, and avoidance of stem or leaf damage. The candidate tests rigid hand-tool alignment, screw-and-nut countertorque, regrasping, and articulated verification.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2106 grades plug depth and tilt, four-sided soil level, fill percentage, spill, firmness under a side push, release, and plant damage. The candidate grades opening angle, locking and retention, three-cycle return, drift, and tool clearance. No material rubric details are missing; the soil-clod and plant-damage approximations are disclosed.
comparisons.reason: Granular backfilling and damage-sensitive stabilization of a plant are meaningfully different from calibrated rigid-mechanism adjustment and locknut retention.

comparisons.objective: Install a circlip in a loose shaft’s groove, rotate it to verify seating, and put down the pliers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Controlled ring spreading with dedicated pliers, shaft stabilization, groove seating, and relative rotation against friction.
comparisons.success_condition: Ring remains undamaged, seated and closed in the groove, rotates at least 15° relative to the restrained shaft, and pliers are removed and released; overspread or bending forces zero.
comparisons.reason: This shares counterholding and a post-installation functional check, but tests elastic retaining-ring installation and relative rotation, not screw-set regulation preserved through concentric jam-nut torque and repeated gripper cycles.

comparisons.objective: Orient and insert an emergency-stop button through a keyed panel hole, then secure it with a rear locking ring.
comparisons.physical_skill: Keyed rotational alignment, through-panel insertion, bimanual front-side stabilization, and rear ring threading.
comparisons.success_condition: Button is seated with its tab aligned, locking ring turns 165–185° and lies within 0.5 mm of the panel, and both parts remain still with grippers clear for one second.
comparisons.reason: It includes bimanual threaded locking, but the setting is a binary keyed panel insertion; it does not regulate a continuous stop angle, counterhold a coupled adjustment screw against locknut reaction, or verify retained actuation.

comparisons.objective: Replace two thin shelf-edge price tickets while preserving the third ticket and nearby cans.
comparisons.physical_skill: Opening a sprung clear strip, extracting nearly flush thin cards, inserting replacements into a narrow channel, and releasing them securely.
comparisons.success_condition: Both old tickets are in the waste tray, matching new tickets are seated under the correct cans, the untouched ticket remains seated, hands withdraw, and the assembly remains still; tipping a can forces zero.
comparisons.reason: This is thin-card extraction and insertion under a sprung cover, with no threaded adjustment, torque preservation, or articulated retention test.

comparisons.objective: Place a phone, watch, and earbuds case on their matching positions of a three-device charger and leave all charging.
comparisons.physical_skill: Multi-object contact/alignment, magnetic placement, flexible watch-band handling, and indicator visibility management.
comparisons.success_condition: Each released device charges uninterrupted for five seconds with a visible indicator while the stand remains within 5 mm and 5° of its starting pose.
comparisons.reason: It tests repeated device placement and charging confirmation rather than coupled screw/nut manipulation or retaining an adjusted mechanical stop.

comparisons.objective: Clamp an aluminium workpiece, drill a marked through-hole on a bench drill press, and leave the machine safe; the candidate adjusts and locks a gripper opening stop, then verifies that setting through repeated actuation.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-776 includes holding a loose plate against clamp-pad rotation, tightening a hold-down screw, operating motor controls and a capstan, and maintaining clearance from a rotating chuck. The candidate instead requires coaxial driver engagement plus wrench engagement on a coupled screw and thin jam nut, bimanual countertorque that preserves a calibrated setting, tool withdrawal, and articulated functional testing.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-776 awards full credit for a clamped plate, a 5 mm through-hole within 5 mm of the punch mark, no hand/wrist entry within 5 cm of the rotating bit or chuck, and a stopped drill with quill raised; partial and spoil outcomes are defined. The candidate grades retained 90° adjustment, nut retention, three repeat cycles, at most 2° drift, and hands/tools clear for one second. No material rubric details are missing from the available versions.
comparisons.reason: Both involve resisting rotation while tightening, but PR-776 uses clamping only as workholding prerequisite for drilling; it does not test coupled adjuster/jam-nut locking where tightening must preserve a setpoint and subsequent mechanism cycles must retain it.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a robot-gripper opening stop, then verifies its setting; PR-1766 clamps locking pliers onto a tube so they remain attached after release.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate needs two-tool coaxial adjustment and countertorque; PR-1766 needs one-gripper transport and squeeze past a spring-latch lock point while avoiding lateral drag.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires accurate angle, seated/retained nuts, three functional cycles and low drift; PR-1766 requires the pliers latched on the marked band, level, unsupported and still. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Although both verify locking after release, the tested mechanisms differ materially: preserving an adjustable screw setting under jam-nut torque versus crossing a handheld pliers latch threshold.

comparisons.objective: Hold a shelf against an irregular wall and trace its profile with a pencil compass; the candidate instead adjusts and locks a gripper stop before testing its retained opening.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1871 requires sustained surface-guided compass motion, simultaneous shelf stabilization, tool orientation, and continuous precision marking. The candidate requires concentric two-tool engagement, coordinated countertorque that prevents screw drift, wrench regrasping, and subsequent lever actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1871 grades a continuous edge-to-edge curved line at 14 stations, profile bend, compass placement, shelf/tool stillness, clearance, and loss events. The candidate grades opening-angle tolerance, locknut seating and retention, repeated-cycle return, drift, and released clearance. All available versions specify the relevant numeric rubric; no material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Although both use two hands and require stabilizing one element while manipulating a tool, tracing a surface profile into a continuous accurate mark is a different tested ability from counterholding a coupled adjustment during locknut tightening and proving retained mechanical function.

comparisons.objective: Attach a detachable handle to a saucepan, prove it load-bearing, carry the pan to a trivet, and release it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Rim/jaw mechanism engagement, latch closure, load-path verification, and stable transport through the attached handle.
comparisons.success_condition: Pan is lifted solely through the locked handle for one second, then placed within 20 mm of the trivet center and released stable for two seconds; direct support, slip, or excessive penetration invalidates credit.
comparisons.reason: Its functional verification is load-bearing transport after latch assembly, not preserving an adjustable stop while tightening a jam nut or checking return angle over repeated cycles.

comparisons.objective: Refit a rack-server air shroud by inserting both front tabs under the fan cage and lowering the rear to seat.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual handling of a large rigid duct, simultaneous dual-tab insertion, constrained lowering, and release among obstacles.
comparisons.success_condition: Both tabs extend at least 3 mm into their slots, all four shroud corners lie within 2 mm of the chassis floor, grippers clear by 3 cm, and the shroud remains still for one second.
comparisons.reason: This tests large-part dual-tab insertion and seating in a server chassis, with no threaded tool use, countertorque regulation, or retained angular-stop calibration.

comparisons.objective: Fit color-matched caps to four pens and sort the completed pens into marked areas; the candidate sets, locks, and functionally verifies an industrial gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-360 tests color matching, repeated coaxial cap insertion, bimanual part handling, release, and sorting. It lacks screw adjustment, wrench/driver countertorque, setpoint preservation during locknut tightening, and articulated retention testing.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-360 gives per-pen credit for a matching cap retained after insertion and hands-clear dwell, plus placement credit when the released capped pen rests inside its color area; full score requires all four capped and sorted. The candidate instead requires specified opening accuracy, installed nuts, three repeat cycles, bounded drift, and released clearance. Available versions disclose that simulated cap retention uses a pose-preserving joint and that physical force qualification is unverified; otherwise the scoring rubric is complete.
comparisons.reason: Generic insertion, bimanual handling, and release are insufficient for overlap: PR-360 measures repeated closure assembly and color sorting, not torque-coupled adjustment locking or preservation of a mechanical setting through functional cycles.

comparisons.objective: Reattach a detached live wrist camera through a tapered sliding shoe and spring-loaded retaining tooth, then release it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Self-referential bimanual alignment, guided insertion into a wrist channel, passive-latch engagement, and retention verification.
comparisons.success_condition: Camera reaches within 5 mm and 5° of its optical target, passes through the guide, seats with the tooth engaged, and remains aligned with the assisting TCP over 80 mm away for two seconds.
comparisons.reason: It tests guided sensor-module insertion and passive latch retention, not an adjustable stop, jam-nut counterholding, or repeated return-angle stability.

comparisons.objective: Candidate calibrates and locks a gripper opening stop; PR-1805 secures a bicycle wheel to a stand with a bent-foot U-lock.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial driver/wrench engagement and rotational counterholding; PR-1805 requires threading a rigid shackle through spokes and around a stand, angled toe insertion, pivoting and two-end crossbar seating.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades retained target angle through repeated motion; PR-1805 grades correct linkage of wheel and stand, bounded two-end latch seating, release clearance and stillness. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Bent-foot two-part lock assembly around fixed objects tests constrained threading and latching, not adjustment preservation against threaded locking torque.

comparisons.objective: Swipe a magnetic-stripe card through a reader at a valid speed and return it to its stand.
comparisons.physical_skill: Orient a thin card, maintain narrow-slot alignment, and execute a continuous speed-bounded pass.
comparisons.success_condition: A single valid read across the encoded span, followed by stable released placement in the stand; extra or failed swipes reduce credit and dropping fails.
comparisons.reason: The candidate tests coupled screw adjustment, jam-nut counterholding, and retained gripper motion; card-slot trajectory control and read completion are different abilities.

comparisons.objective: PR-1882 joins articulated chain ends with a connecting link and side-entry keeper; the candidate sets a gripper opening limit.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1882 tests multi-hole alignment and lateral keeper insertion into a loose chain assembly, not coupled screw-and-nut counterholding.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1882 requires both ends seated, keeper retained, joint cradled, chain guided, and hands released; the candidate requires a locked angle surviving three cycles.
comparisons.reason: Although both include retention, chain-link assembly does not test preserving a calibrated setting against jam-nut tightening reaction.

comparisons.objective: PR-1961 fills and strikes three drywall holes flush; the candidate adjusts and locks robot-gripper hardware.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1961 tests loading, packing, and angle-controlled wiping with a putty knife, unlike coaxial driver seating and wrench countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1961 measures filled-hole depth, proud material, surface damage, and knife set-down; the candidate measures retained opening angle, locking, and repeat cycles.
comparisons.reason: Material deposition and surface finishing are unrelated to coupled threaded adjustment and functional retention.

comparisons.objective: Install a bakery-mixer beater and guard, raise the bowl, run the mixer, and stop it safely.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bayonet-style hub alignment and insertion against a spring collar, guard placement, lever operation, and guarded functional operation.
comparisons.success_condition: Retained beater and guard, raised bowl, five seconds of specified rotation, then a stopped and released assembly with clear hands.
comparisons.reason: Both include post-assembly functional verification, but the mixer task tests bayonet insertion and guarded operation rather than preserving an adjustable stop while tightening its concentric locknut.

comparisons.objective: PR-1916 lays two robot cables into a carrier and snaps twelve crossbars shut; the candidate adjusts gripper hardware.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1916 tests cable routing, ordering, seating, and repeated snap-latching without strain-relief damage; the candidate tests rigid tool use and coupled torque control.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1916 requires both cables correctly routed through every closed link with adequate tails and release; the candidate requires a locked 90° stop surviving cycles.
comparisons.reason: Robot-related context is shared, but cable routing and distributed latching do not measure screw-setting preservation.

comparisons.objective: PR-1924 lands a hoisted motor over four studs while operating a pendant; the candidate adjusts a gripper stop on a bench fixture.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1924 tests suspended-load steering, four-hole alignment, and simultaneous hold-to-run control under pinch constraints, not two-tool countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1924 requires all feet seated, chain slack, controls released, and no unsafe load interaction; the candidate requires locked angular retention over three cycles.
comparisons.reason: Precision landing of a swinging heavy load is meaningfully different from threaded calibration and locknut tightening.

comparisons.objective: PR-2153 refits a refrigerator door bin onto two concealed supports; the candidate calibrates and locks a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2153 tests level bimanual carrying, simultaneous support engagement, and downward seating, not driver/wrench coordination.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2153 requires both ends engaged and locked, level, still, and released; the candidate requires a specified angle, retained nuts, low drift, and repeated actuation.
comparisons.reason: Dual-support placement and seating do not test preserving an adjustable threaded setting under tightening reaction.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts a DRG 80 gripper’s opening-stop screw to 90°, locks the setting with a jam nut, and verifies retained opening through repeated cold-lever cycles. PR 2245 instead removes a loose screwdriver from a control box, shuts and latches its cover, and safely switches on a test supply.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests coaxial driver and thin-wrench seating, simultaneous screw counterholding and nut tightening without disturbing an angular setting, tool regrasping/withdrawal, and articulated functional verification. PR 2245 tests loose-tool extraction and placement, hinged-cover closure, catch engagement, rocker actuation, and safe sequencing. They share only generic grasping, tool handling, and mechanism actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate scores measured opening accuracy, locknut/second-nut retention, one then three repeatable close-open cycles, limited stop drift, and released-tool clearance, with loss conditions for missing hardware, dropped tools, fixture displacement, or invalid motion. PR 2245 scores the screwdriver removed, resting and released on the table, the cover shut and latched, safe switch-on, and gripper clearance; unsafe energization permanently forces zero. Both available PR 2245 spec versions state the same substantive rubric.
comparisons.reason: The tested ability is meaningfully different: preserving a calibrated mechanical stop while applying coupled countertorque and proving adjustment retention is not tested by enclosure housekeeping, latching, and safe re-energization. Different industrial settings alone are not the basis for distinction.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks an angular gripper stop; PR-2258 squares a racked wooden face frame without moving it off its marks.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses coaxial tools and coordinated countertorque; PR-2258 applies opposed bimanual forces to rack a compliant four-joint frame while preventing gross sliding.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a locked angle and repeatable cycles; PR-2258 requires nearly equal diagonals, closed joints, location retention and released stillness.
comparisons.reason: Opposed-force coordination is generic, while the controlled mechanisms and measured outcomes are unrelated; all material rubric details are present.

comparisons.objective: PR-1520 joins furniture panels by orienting two eccentric cams, aligning and inserting a shelf over bolts/dowels, then locking the joint. The candidate calibrates and locks a robot-gripper opening stop, then verifies retained motion.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1520 tests panel alignment/insertion and sequential screwdriver operation of two cams. The candidate tests simultaneous concentric hex-driver and thin-wrench countertorque so jam-nut tightening does not disturb a screw-defined angle, followed by articulated cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1520 requires both bolt heads captured, cams rotated at least 120°, joint gap ≤0.5 mm, tools returned, and hands clear; its body also makes forceful insertion against a closed cam a zero-score damage state. The candidate requires a 90° setting within 3°, retained nuts, ≤2° drift through three cycles, tool withdrawal, and 30 mm clearance for one second. No material rubric detail is missing for this comparison.
comparisons.reason: Both involve rotary tools and locking, but PR-1520 primarily tests connector orientation plus panel insertion and eccentric latching, not preserving an adjustable stop under locknut reaction and validating retained mechanism motion.

comparisons.objective: PR-1775 refits a loaded drawer onto roller slides and pull-tests it; the candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1775 tests elevated insertion past rear hooks, bilateral rail seating, closing, and controlled reopening, not tool-mediated countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1775 requires the drawer on both slides, a prior released closure, and a final 30–80 mm opening; the candidate requires a locked target angle retained across cycles.
comparisons.reason: The drawer's pull test verifies rail engagement, not preservation of a calibrated screw setting.

comparisons.objective: Candidate preserves and locks one adjustable robot-gripper stop, then verifies motion; PR-1968 opens three breaker clamps, inserts a comb busbar and tightens all terminal screws.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires simultaneous driver counterholding and thin-nut tightening on one coupled adjustment; PR-1968 requires repeated screwdriver turning plus multi-pin alignment and insertion.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires retained angular calibration over three cycles; PR-1968 requires three inserted and tightened pins that resist a 10 N pull with hands and tool clear.
comparisons.reason: Both use a screwdriver, but terminal preparation and multi-pin busbar fastening do not test locking an adjustable screw without disturbing its setting; no rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Uncork a wine bottle while it remains in its cradle.
comparisons.physical_skill: Drive a corkscrew into a cork, operate its lever mechanism, and resist extraction forces without displacing the bottle.
comparisons.success_condition: Cork fully removed and displaced from the mouth while the bottle stays within cradle pose limits; partial credit covers penetration and partial extraction.
comparisons.reason: Shared rotary tool motion and reaction management are generic; cork penetration and high-force extraction do not test precision stop setting, jam-nut countertorque, or retained actuation.

comparisons.objective: Calibrate a colorimeter using the correct blank, measure a sample at a requested wavelength, and return both cuvettes.
comparisons.physical_skill: Select and orient cuvettes, insert them into a tight well, operate controls and hood, and perform reference-dependent sequencing.
comparisons.success_condition: A stable valid sample reading after correct blank calibration, followed by both released cuvettes in separate rack pockets; drops latch failure.
comparisons.reason: This tests reference-dependent instrument operation and cuvette orientation, not mechanical adjustment, locking against reaction torque, or repeated articulated verification.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks a gripper opening limit; PR-1151 purges air from a syringe while preserving liquid and returns it to a rack.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires tool seating, threaded countertorque and articulated verification; PR-1151 requires orienting a fluid-filled syringe, stabilizing its barrel and regulating plunger travel.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate measures retained angle, drift, nut retention and cycle function; PR-1151 measures residual air, liquid loss, safe pose, release and a continuous endpoint hold.
comparisons.reason: Fluid-preserving plunger control is meaningfully different from mechanical stop adjustment and locknut counterholding; all spec revisions provide sufficient rubric detail.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop; PR-1870 removes a drawer by operating two opposite-sense slide releases and sets it down.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses two coaxial tools for countertorque; PR-1870 simultaneously presses opposed latch levers while pulling and supporting a free drawer.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a retained 90° setting through three cycles; PR-1870 requires the drawer fully off both slides, flat, still and released on the table.
comparisons.reason: Bimanual coordination is shared only at a generic level; drawer unlatching and load removal do not test threaded setting preservation, and no rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: PR-1923 threads shock cord through a spring cord lock while depressing its button; the candidate sets a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1923 tests sustained button actuation coordinated with deformable threading and release to spring grip; the candidate tests rigid concentric tool seating and countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1923 requires specified cord protrusion, spring-only retention, table rest, and released hands; the candidate requires a locked angle retained through three cycles.
comparisons.reason: Holding open a spring passage during cord insertion does not measure calibrated screw adjustment or jam-nut locking.

comparisons.objective: Candidate locks a robot-gripper opening adjustment and verifies it; PR-1951 performs the squeeze-turn-wait-and-withdraw step of a rapid strep test.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires driver/wrench seating and countertorque; PR-1951 maintains a moving squeeze on a soft tube while repeatedly regrasping and turning a swab.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires angular accuracy and low drift over cycles; PR-1951 requires five net turns, a timed dwell, continuously squeezed rotating withdrawal and disposal.
comparisons.reason: Maintaining deformable-tube squeeze during swab rotation and withdrawal is not the same ability as locknut-secured stop adjustment; all material rubric details are present.

comparisons.objective: PR-2061 mixes layered liquid in two open tubes without spilling; the candidate sets and locks gripper hardware.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2061 tests controlled tube motion, liquid mixing, spill avoidance, and rack insertion, not threaded tool use.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2061 requires both solutions mixed, no spill, both tubes racked, released, and still; the candidate requires a retained 90° stop over repeated cycles.
comparisons.reason: Fluid mixing under a spill constraint is unrelated to mechanical stop calibration and countertorque.

comparisons.objective: PR-2103 opens a robot vacuum brush door by releasing two catches; the candidate adjusts a robot gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2103 tests simultaneous dual-button compression followed by hinged-door lifting while stabilizing the appliance; the candidate tests two-tool screw/nut coordination.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2103 requires the door open at least 80°, appliance in place, hands clear, and still; the candidate requires a locked target angle and repeat-cycle retention.
comparisons.reason: Opening a dual-catch access door is not an adjustable-setting or locknut-retention task.

comparisons.objective: PR-1562 makes a copper-pipe compression joint; the candidate adjusts and locks a robot-gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1562 tests ordering an olive and nut, seating pipe, finding snug, and tightening with a spanner; the candidate tests coaxial driver seating plus simultaneous jam-nut counterholding to prevent setting drift.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1562 requires pipe home, olive captured, and nut 3/4–1 1/4 turns past calibrated snug without over-compression; the candidate requires a retained 90° angle after three actuation cycles.
comparisons.reason: This is a close threaded-tool neighbor, but controlled compression-joint makeup neither preserves an independent screw setting nor verifies articulated travel.

comparisons.objective: PR-2029 seats a Mini-ITX motherboard on four standoffs with rear I/O aligned; the candidate sets a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2029 tests delicate planar handling and simultaneous four-hole plus port alignment, not driver/wrench countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2029 requires every mounting hole seated, ports in the opening, board still, and grippers released; fastening and operation are explicitly excluded, unlike the candidate's lock and cycle test.
comparisons.reason: Motherboard seating ready for fastening is a multi-feature placement ability, not calibrated stop locking.

comparisons.objective: PR-2052 sets and locks a jigsaw shoe at a 45° bevel; the candidate sets and locks a gripper stop at 90° and verifies retained motion.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2052 requires releasing a lever, sliding off a positive stop, tilting through detents, and reclamping; the candidate requires simultaneous coaxial driver and thin-wrench countertorque on a screw/jam-nut pair.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2052 requires a hands-off 45° shoe with its lever clamped and stable under a push; the candidate additionally requires both nuts retained and three close-open cycles returning within tolerance and drift limits.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest objective-level match, but the locking mechanism and core tested ability differ meaningfully: detent-and-lever repositioning versus preserving a threaded adjustment against tightening reaction and proving cyclic retention.

comparisons.objective: PR-2077 transfers four instruments onto a sterile field without contamination; the candidate adjusts and locks robot hardware.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2077 tests collision-free carrying, placement within a sterile boundary, spacing, and contamination-aware hand use, not threaded torque control.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2077 requires all instruments flat, separated, sterile, released, and still; the candidate requires angular accuracy, locking, retained cycles, and tool clearance.
comparisons.reason: Sterility-preserving placement tests contact avoidance rather than mechanical calibration.

comparisons.objective: PR-2164 function-tests a seat-belt retractor by slow payout, jerk locking, sustained pull, and controlled rewind; the candidate adjusts and function-tests a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2164 tests acceleration-sensitive webbing manipulation, tension maintenance, and controlled retraction; the candidate tests two-tool threaded adjustment and countertorque followed by lever actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2164 requires ordered payout, lock within 25 mm, sustained load, gentle return, release, and dwell; the candidate requires a locked 90° stop with bounded drift across three cycles.
comparisons.reason: Both include functional cycling, but the seat-belt task tests inertial-lock behavior and tension control, not setting and retaining an adjustable mechanical stop.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets a gripper’s adjustable opening stop, locks the setting, and verifies retention through repeated actuation; PR 2242 exposes and scans a barcode on a sprung training forearm, then restores the scanner and arm.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests coaxial driver/wrench seating, bimanual screw counterholding against locknut torque, tool regrasping, and retained mechanical adjustment. PR 2242 tests continuously holding a return-sprung limb while the other hand grasps, triggers, aims, and replaces a scanner, with gentle limb handling.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a locked 90° opening within tolerance, three repeatable cycles, limited drift, retained nuts, tool removal, and clearance dwell. PR 2242 requires a valid timed barcode read within the scanner envelope, speed-safe forearm motion, scanner replacement, palm-down restoration, and release clearance. Both rubrics provide numeric thresholds; no material comparison detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: The shared bimanual stabilization primitive supports different tested abilities: preserving a coupled mechanical adjustment against tightening reaction and proving its retained function is meaningfully different from maintaining a sprung limb orientation while operating an optical instrument and safely restoring the scene.

comparisons.objective: Load a card under a clipboard clip and prove that the spring clamp retains it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a sprung lever open with one hand while sliding and aligning a thin sheet with the other, then release and lift the board.
comparisons.success_condition: Card clamped at the stop and square, released, and retained during a 60-degree tilt with no more than 3 mm slip.
comparisons.reason: Although both use asymmetric bimanual coordination and retention verification, the clipboard tests sustained spring opening plus sheet insertion, not concentric driver-and-wrench counterholding.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a robot-gripper opening stop; PR-125 aligns mating flanges and inserts locating pins.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires concentric threaded-tool counterholding; PR-125 requires holding flange faces and holes aligned while inserting horizontal pins.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate succeeds on a locked 90° setting retained through three cycles; PR-125 succeeds on flange-axis alignment and correctly seated pins.
comparisons.reason: Both involve bimanual assembly, but flange alignment and pin insertion do not test preserving a threaded adjustment during jam-nut locking; no rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Candidate locks an adjusted robot-gripper stop; PR-1868 connects a hose nipple to a sprung quick-connect coupler.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate counterholds a screw while tightening its jam nut; PR-1868 retracts a sprung collar while aligning and inserting a flexible-hose fitting, then releases it to latch.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires retained angle and repeatable articulated motion; PR-1868 requires seated pawl engagement, collar return, pull retention, stillness and hand clearance.
comparisons.reason: Both culminate in hands-off retention, but quick-connect insertion under collar spring load does not test locknut preservation of an adjustable setting; no rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Tighten a nylon-insert locknut in a slot that permits only a 44-degree wrench swing.
comparisons.physical_skill: Seat an open-end wrench, make repeated short strokes, flip or reindex it between bites, and overcome nut drag.
comparisons.success_condition: Nut rotated up to 178 degrees and seated for one second, with partial credit based on net tightening angle.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest record by hardware, but it tests repeated wrench reindexing on one nut; the candidate tests preserving a separately adjusted screw with a coaxial driver while locking a jam nut, followed by retained-motion cycles.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts a gripper stop; PR-1243 greases a pivot through a nipple without leakage.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses coupled screw/nut countertorque; PR-1243 maintains a sealed coupler while pumping repeated lever strokes.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades retained opening angle and cycles; PR-1243 grades sealing, four grease shots, absence of leakage, and tool return.
comparisons.reason: Shared bimanual stabilization is generic; the tested contact, force-control, and outcome mechanisms differ.

comparisons.objective: Move an untaped-bottom carton of cans onto a shelf without losing its contents.
comparisons.physical_skill: Discover and continuously support hinged bottom flaps from below while carrying and placing the carton bimanually.
comparisons.success_condition: All cans remain inside throughout, and the carton is released upright and stable on the shelf; any escaped can permanently scores zero.
comparisons.reason: Continuous load support during transport is unrelated to coupled rotary adjustment, countertorque locking, and functional cycling.

comparisons.objective: Use a tong puller to remove a midget fuse from an open-clip block and place it in a tray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Align and close a sprung puller around a small cylindrical fuse in tight clearance, extract it, release it, and put the tool down.
comparisons.success_condition: Target fuse released and still in the tray with the puller set down; disturbing neighboring fuses fails and tool-free extraction caps credit.
comparisons.reason: Precision tool seating is shared only generically; fuse grasp-and-extraction does not test adjustment preservation, jam-nut reaction, or post-lock actuation.

comparisons.objective: Install a spring cage nut into a marked rack-rail hole from behind.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hook one cage lip, hold and rotate the nut, and compress the opposite spring lip with a screwdriver until it passes the square hole.
comparisons.success_condition: Both lips sprung out around the marked hole, nut centered and flat, tools and hands withdrawn, and the assembly still for the required dwell; drops, wrong holes, or bent lips fail.
comparisons.reason: Both are bimanual tool operations, but cage-nut installation tests spring-lip compression and insertion through a panel rather than coupled screw setting and countertorque locking.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop; PR-312 replaces a ratchet-dispenser cartridge and restores the tool.
comparisons.physical_skill: Concentric countertorque differs from rod retraction, cartridge extraction/insertion, pawl re-engagement, and cradle placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks retained angle over cycles; PR-312 checks used-cartridge collection, replacement seating, rod engagement, and released clearance.
comparisons.reason: The ratchet task tests component replacement and mechanism restoration, not preservation of an adjusted setting while locking.

comparisons.objective: Candidate configures a gripper; PR-709 samples a handhole atmosphere before conditionally removing cover bolts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate emphasizes simultaneous driver/wrench torque control; PR-709 emphasizes hose placement, a 60-second sample, alarm-conditioned decisions, and bolt removal.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks retained motion; PR-709 checks valid sampling and either preserved closure or two removed bolts based on the alarm.
comparisons.reason: The handhole task tests safety-conditioned inspection and access, not adjustment retention.

comparisons.objective: Tighten a tourniquet windlass against rollback until a gauge is green, snap the rod into its clip, and release it; candidate sets and jam-nut-locks a gripper opening stop before cycling it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both involve loaded rotary adjustment and locking, but PR-1026 requires windlass regrasping and rod snap-in while preserving band tension; candidate requires simultaneous coaxial driver counterholding and thin-nut wrench tightening without shifting a precision screw setting.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1026 succeeds when pressure is at least 250 mmHg, the rod is clipped, and the robot clears it for one second; candidate requires a 90° retained stop, at most 2° drift across three cycles, both nuts retained, and one-second 30 mm clearance.
comparisons.reason: Shared adjust-lock-release primitives do not erase the meaningful difference between regrasping and clipping a rollback-loaded windlass versus two-tool screw/jam-nut countertorque followed by repeated functional retention testing; the record supplies complete thresholds and failure tiers.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts gripper travel; PR-1087 opens a bottle through a safety loop and rocker latch.
comparisons.physical_skill: Two-tool screw/nut counterholding differs from sequential detent release, rocker actuation, and bottle stabilization.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires retained opening after cycles; PR-1087 requires lid opening while maintaining bottle support and force limits.
comparisons.reason: The bottle task tests unlatching and opening, not locking an adjustable setting.

comparisons.objective: Align and cut a card to width on a guillotine while keeping the free gripper clear of the blade; candidate adjusts, locks, and functionally verifies a robot-gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1135 tests planar card alignment, holding material flat, guarded handle operation, and hazard-zone avoidance; candidate tests precision rotary tool seating, bimanual countertorque, locknut tightening, and test-lever actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1135 requires an 8 cm cut within 5 mm, blade down, released card, safe hand clearance, and stillness; candidate requires retained angular accuracy through three cycles, nut retention, tool withdrawal, and clearance.
comparisons.reason: Neither the physical mechanism nor the graded ability overlaps beyond generic bimanual manipulation; all available versions state the cutting proxy, real-bench measurement, safety revocation, partial credit, and dwell details.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop; PR-1444 sets a spring rat trap without allowing a snap or exposing a gripper to the strike path.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate applies coordinated threaded countertorque; PR-1444 restrains a spring-loaded hammer while positioning and latching a separate lock bar.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires retained angle over three cycles with tools clear; PR-1444 requires the hammer latched back, no snap or unsafe strike-path exposure, and arms clear.
comparisons.reason: Both coordinate against a reaction load, but trap setting tests spring restraint and hazard-aware latching rather than locknut-preserved adjustment; no rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks a robot-gripper motion limit; PR-1849 gauges seven machined blocks and sorts them by dimensional tolerance.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial tool seating and countertorque; PR-1849 requires repeated alignment with GO and NO-GO gaps, released gauge checks and sorting.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a retained target angle and functional cycles; PR-1849 requires valid ordered gauge checks and correct final tray classification, with escapes penalized.
comparisons.reason: Dimensional inspection and classification do not test threaded stop locking or retention under cycling; all material rubric details are present.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets gripper travel; PR-1864 aligns and press-fits a servo horn onto a splined shaft.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coupled screw/nut countertorque differs from fine angular registration followed by axial spline insertion.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate verifies locking and cyclic retention; PR-1864 verifies correct spline index, flush seating, stillness, and released clearance.
comparisons.reason: Both use angular alignment, but one tests indexed insertion while the other tests preservation of an adjustable stop during locking.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts a robot gripper; PR-1872 secures a carton to a luggage cart with a bungee.
comparisons.physical_skill: Driver/wrench countertorque differs from stretching flexible cord and engaging hooks against elastic pull.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires retained angle over cycles; PR-1872 requires both hooks home and carton retention throughout a cart-motion test.
comparisons.reason: Their mechanisms and tested manipulation abilities differ beyond shared retention testing.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a gripper opening stop; PR-1935 couples a scaffold transom by positioning it, closing a cap, swinging a bolt and running down its nut.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate must counterhold an adjustment screw while tightening a concentric jam nut; PR-1935 supports and aligns a long tube, operates a hinged cap and bolt, and spins a single fastening nut.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires preserved angle and repeated motion after release; PR-1935 requires the transom on its mark, square, capped, bolted, gripped and hands clear.
comparisons.reason: Running down a scaffold fastener does not require preserving a calibrated screw position against its locknut or verifying retained articulated travel; no rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Candidate configures gripper motion; PR-1975 removes an interrupted suture.
comparisons.physical_skill: Mechanical countertorque differs from forceps lifting, flush cutting, controlled extraction toward a wound, and instrument return.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks locked cyclic travel; PR-1975 checks safe cut location, complete extraction, wound protection, disposal, and tool release.
comparisons.reason: No meaningful objective, mechanism, or success-condition overlap exists.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks a gripper opening stop; PR-2112 rotates a hose-wand dial from Jet to Shower.
comparisons.physical_skill: Two-tool counterholding under tightening reaction differs from stabilizing a wand while turning a detented selector dial.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a locked setting retained over three cycles; PR-2112 requires the Shower detent selected and the wand released still on the bench.
comparisons.reason: Target-angle selection is shared superficially, but the hose task lacks separate locking, countertorque, and functional-cycle retention.

comparisons.objective: Candidate configures a robot gripper; the board task selects conveyor parts and builds a pictured model.
comparisons.physical_skill: Countertorque and tool control differ from time-constrained interception, look-alike discrimination, temporary parking, and stacking.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks retained opening motion; the board task checks a four-part structure, rejected extras exiting downstream, and no conveyor jam.
comparisons.reason: The board record contains a complete numeric rubric, and its tested ability is unrelated to mechanical adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts a gripper stop; PR-54 seats an access panel and installs two retainer bars.
comparisons.physical_skill: Concentric screw/nut countertorque differs from planar panel insertion and bar placement into rib slots.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires locked angular repeatability; PR-54 requires a flush panel and one or two correctly seated retainer bars.
comparisons.reason: Both secure a component, but the panel task tests geometric seating rather than force-coupled adjustment locking.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets a gripper opening limit; PR-1800 inserts an oil-feed sleeve with its radial passage registered.
comparisons.physical_skill: Driver/wrench countertorque differs from tight coaxial insertion with rotational port alignment.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate verifies lock retention through repeated motion; PR-1800 verifies released supported seating and an unobstructed oil-passage gauge envelope for one second.
comparisons.reason: PR-1800 explicitly ends before locking, so it does not test preservation of a setting during locknut tightening or subsequent cycling.

comparisons.objective: Load an IV-set fitment and safety clamp into a pump; the candidate sets and locks a gripper opening stop, then tests it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Keyed seating of two parts joined by soft tubing versus concentric driver-and-wrench countertorque that preserves a screw setting.
comparisons.success_condition: Fitment and clamp seated without twist or stretch, then released; candidate requires a locked 90° opening retained through three cycles with tools clear.
comparisons.reason: Soft-tube-guided insertion and clamp seating do not test adjustable-stop preservation under jam-nut reaction or post-lock cycling.

comparisons.objective: Candidate calibrates and locks an angular gripper stop; PR-2015 turns a suspended humanoid upper body half a revolution and brings it gently to rest.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses precise two-tool countertorque and later cycles a mechanism; PR-2015 regulates the momentum of a freely yawing 18.3 kg suspended assembly through push and catch actions.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a locked 90° opening with low drift over three cycles; PR-2015 requires approximately 180° net rotation, under 1°/s for one second, without blows or collisions.
comparisons.reason: Both concern robot hardware, but suspended-load momentum control is a different tested ability from threaded stop adjustment; all material rubric details are present.

comparisons.objective: Install a telescoping server rail between the front and rear rack flanges at the marked U.
comparisons.physical_skill: Carry a long rail, align two peg pairs, latch the rear, extend the slide, and latch the front level at the matching U.
comparisons.success_condition: Both ends latched at the marked U, rail within 0.5 degrees of level, hands clear for two seconds; a reversed or fallen rail fails.
comparisons.reason: This tests long-part alignment, telescoping extension, and dual-end latching, not rotary setting preservation or jam-nut counterholding.

comparisons.objective: Stow three cases while keeping load off a fragile case; the candidate configures a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Packing, stacking, and rule-aware placement versus two-tool adjustment and locknut counterholding.
comparisons.success_condition: All cases lie correctly in two bays with no forbidden stack; candidate requires a locked target angle and repeated functional return.
comparisons.reason: The tested packing and load-path planning ability is unrelated to preserving a mechanical setting during locking.

comparisons.objective: Insert and center a U-joint cross between opposed yoke bores; the candidate sets and locks an angular stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Overtravel, swing alignment, and bilateral bore insertion versus screw adjustment with wrench/driver countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: Both journals are centered in their holes and still; candidate requires target angle, retained nuts, three cycles, low drift, and tool clearance.
comparisons.reason: Both involve alignment, but the record tests constrained rigid insertion rather than torque-coupled calibration and retention.

comparisons.objective: Free a fused print-in-place hinge without breaking it; the candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated sub-breakage rocking to overcome adhesion versus coaxial tool use and reaction-counterholding during locknut tightening.
comparisons.success_condition: Leaf reaches 120° and passes a low-force free-motion test; candidate returns to 90° through three cycles with the setting locked.
comparisons.reason: The indexed record has no task.json/spec versions, but its complete PR body defines a break-free rocking test that is meaningfully different from setting retention.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a robot-gripper stop; PR-1276 reloads a spring-return long-arm stapler and staples two sheets.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires simultaneous driver and wrench control; PR-1276 holds a sprung magazine open, inserts and seats a staple strip, handles paper and presses the stapler.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires angular retention and repeatable cycles; PR-1276 requires the stapler loaded, sheets physically stapled together, mechanisms still and arms clear.
comparisons.reason: Holding a magazine open during loading and subsequently firing a staple does not test preserving a screw adjustment during jam-nut locking; no rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Produce a sound TIG bead with torch and filler rod; the candidate sets and verifies a mechanical opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Continuous bimanual heat-path and filler control versus discrete screw adjustment, jam-nut countertorque, and tool withdrawal.
comparisons.success_condition: All seam segments are sound without contamination or burn-through and tools are returned; candidate requires angle accuracy and cycle retention.
comparisons.reason: Weld-process control and bead quality do not test preservation of an adjustable stop under locking torque.

comparisons.objective: Clip a pulse oximeter onto an index finger without moving the hand; the candidate configures a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Spring-clip squeeze-slide-release with hand stabilization versus coaxial adjustment and locknut counterholding.
comparisons.success_condition: Oximeter is seated, correctly oriented, released, and the hand remains near its mark; candidate requires locked angle retention through cycles.
comparisons.reason: Spring-clip placement on a supported finger is a different physical ability from torque-coupled mechanical calibration.

comparisons.objective: Snap a sip lid fully around a filled paper cup; the candidate sets and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Progressive circumferential pressing while avoiding cup tip or wall crush versus two-tool angular adjustment and countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: All eight lid sectors are seated with the cup intact and hands clear; candidate requires a precise retained opening over repeated actuation.
comparisons.reason: Distributed snap-fit seating under container-damage constraints does not overlap the candidate's adjustable-stop retention ability.

comparisons.objective: Heat-shrink a sleeve uniformly over a cable lug; the candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Timed noncontact heat exposure with cable rotation versus seated wrench/driver use and reaction-counterholding.
comparisons.success_condition: All sleeve stations recover without char or contact and the gun is safely stowed; candidate requires locked angular accuracy and low cycle drift.
comparisons.reason: The record tests controlled thermal processing, not coupled mechanical adjustment and functional retention.

comparisons.objective: Stow a screwdriver while preventing a two-drawer tool chest from tipping; the candidate configures a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Drawer sequencing, chest stability management, and object placement versus tool seating and countertorque on a screw/jam nut.
comparisons.success_condition: Screwdriver rests in the right drawer without chest tip or drag; candidate retains the target opening through three cycles.
comparisons.reason: Tip-over avoidance during drawer use is unrelated to adjustable-stop calibration and locking.

comparisons.objective: Level and pin-lock a see-saw platform before loading it; the candidate sets and locknuts a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Supporting an articulated platform and inserting a transverse safety pin versus concentric screw adjustment and nut counterholding.
comparisons.success_condition: Platform is level, pin traverses both walls and lug, blocks are placed, and the hand is untouched; candidate requires retained 90° cycling.
comparisons.reason: Both include a lock, but the record tests safety-pin alignment and load sequencing rather than preserving a calibrated setting against tightening reaction.

comparisons.objective: Replace a toilet roll and reseat a spring spindle in two sockets; the candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Compressing a telescoping spindle while steering its free end into a socket versus coaxial driver/wrench countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: New roll hangs on a released spindle with both ends seated; candidate requires a locked target opening retained across three cycles.
comparisons.reason: Spring-spindle compression and bilateral socket insertion do not test locknut-induced setting disturbance or calibration retention.

comparisons.objective: Open a can with a handheld rotary opener; the candidate sets and locks a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Maintain handle squeeze while repeatedly regrasping and turning a feed key versus hold a driver setting while tightening a concentric jam nut.
comparisons.success_condition: Lid is cut all around, opener removed, and can upright; candidate requires a precise locked angle and repeated return with low drift.
comparisons.reason: The tasks share generic bimanual hold-and-turn primitives, but continuous cutting under clamp force is meaningfully different from preserving an adjustable setting during locknut tightening.

comparisons.objective: Seat a robot-controller add-on board onto two pin rows without bending pins; the candidate configures a robot gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fine multi-pin leveling and even axial insertion versus screw-angle adjustment, wrench seating, and countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: Board is fully seated, unbent, still, and released; candidate must hold a locked 90° opening through three functional cycles.
comparisons.reason: Both concern robot assembly, but the record tests precision connector insertion rather than adjustable-stop calibration and retention.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks a gripper opening stop; PR-1956 breaks a cocktail-shaker seal and separates the tins without spilling.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires concentric driver-and-wrench countertorque that preserves an angular setting; PR-1956 requires holding one tin and delivering a correctly placed impact before lifting the other.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a locked 90° setting, limited drift, three repeatable cycles, retained hardware, and released clearance; PR-1956 requires blow-caused seal release, separated upright tins, clear hands, and no dent, spill, or loss.
comparisons.reason: Placed impact and spill-safe vessel separation do not test coupled screw adjustment, locknut reaction control, or post-lock functional retention; both rubrics provide material numeric details.

comparisons.objective: Spike an IV bag and prime its drip chamber to a target liquid level; the candidate sets and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Aseptic cap removal, axial spike insertion, chamber positioning, and controlled squeezing versus coaxial driver/wrench counterholding.
comparisons.success_condition: Spike is seated and liquid length is 15–27 mm without contamination or overfill; candidate requires retained angular calibration through three cycles.
comparisons.reason: Fluid-level priming and sterile insertion do not test preservation of a screw setting against locking torque.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop at 90°; PR-2142 opens a keyless drill chuck, removes its bit, and deposits the bit in a tray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both involve bimanual reaction control, but the candidate must keep a driver seated while a concentric jam nut is tightened without rotating the adjusted screw; PR-2142 counterholds a loose drill while hand-turning its sleeve, then extracts the bit.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate scores retained angle and repeated articulated cycles after both tools are withdrawn; PR-2142 scores the bit wholly outside the chuck, safely supported or tray-contained, with the drill and objects released and still.
comparisons.reason: PR-2142 tests chuck release and extraction, not preservation of a calibrated screw phase against its locknut's tightening reaction or subsequent motion verification; no material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Transfer and seat a strut across keep-out obstacles; the candidate sets and locks a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Obstacle-aware carrying, staged bimanual handoff, and tight saddle placement versus driver/wrench countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: Strut is seated while the witness housing remains undisturbed; candidate requires a precise locked opening retained through cycling.
comparisons.reason: Keep-out routing and handoff are different from torque-coupled calibration and functional retention.

comparisons.objective: Recover a clothing-obstructed drawer and open it fully; the candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Detect a jam, compress a spring-like clothing proxy, and resume drawer travel versus coaxial screw/nut adjustment with countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: Ordered jam, compression, clearance, and full-opening milestones culminate in a still drawer; candidate requires locked angle and repeated retained motion.
comparisons.reason: The indexed record has no task.json/spec versions, but its complete PR body establishes obstruction recovery, not adjustable-stop calibration.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks an angular-gripper stop; PR-741 inserts a stripped cable into a lug, actuates a crimping press, removes the terminated cable, and returns it to its rest.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires two concentric tools and countertorque during locking; PR-741 requires depth-and-axis-controlled cable insertion held while another hand closes a lever press.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires retained 90° opening over three cycles with low drift and retained nuts; PR-741 requires prescribed insertion depth and alignment at crimp, release, removal, rest placement, and in later versions a real pull test.
comparisons.reason: Holding an inserted cable while operating a crimper does not test locking a continuous adjustment against coupled jam-nut torque or retained articulated motion; all spec versions state observable criteria.

comparisons.objective: Open a locker while catching a box leaning on its door, then stand it on a mat; the candidate configures a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Support-transfer through a partially opened door and upright transport versus seated tools, countertorque, and angular adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Box is never dropped or tipped and finishes upright on the mat; candidate requires locked target angle and repeated functional return.
comparisons.reason: Hidden-load recovery and safe transport do not test coupled screw-and-locknut calibration.

comparisons.objective: Candidate calibrates and locks a gripper opening stop; PR-984 centers an inside-bolt-circle gasket between flanges and inserts four bolts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate emphasizes coaxial tool seating, wrench regrasping, and countertorque; PR-984 emphasizes planar gasket insertion and centering in a constrained gap followed by repeated bolt-through-hole placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires locked angle retention and repeatable close-open cycles; PR-984 requires the gasket centered and flat, the upper flange undisturbed, all four bolts seated through both flanges, release, and dwell.
comparisons.reason: Gasket alignment and multi-bolt insertion do not exercise coupled adjustment-and-locking reaction control; the absence of modeled threads or torque in PR-984 further separates the tested ability, and its rubric is detailed.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a robot-gripper opening limit; PR-1896 reads tire pressure through a Schrader valve with a pencil gauge and returns the gauge to its holder.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires concentric two-tool torque coordination; PR-1896 requires square axial gauge seating, controlled valve-core depression, a timed seal, and replacement of the gauge.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a retained angular setting over three cycles; PR-1896 requires a sealed 1.5-second press, a 33–37 psi stick reading, upright holder placement, release, and stillness.
comparisons.reason: Pressure-gauge sealing and reading do not test locking an adjustable stop against fastening reaction or post-lock articulated repeatability; no material rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks a gripper opening stop; PR-1906 performs an insulin-pen safety shot and then dials a 12-unit dose.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses a hex driver and thin-nut wrench with coordinated countertorque; PR-1906 requires cap removal, repeated dose-knob regrasping, visual unit correction, axial injection-force control, and safe needle orientation.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires retained 90° opening through three cycles; PR-1906 requires a completed 2-unit safety shot with the needle up and a five-second hold, then a displayed 12-unit setting, safe tray placement, and clearance.
comparisons.reason: Dose dialing and priming a medical pen are not equivalent to coupled screw-and-locknut calibration or functional retention testing; the record supplies numeric outcome and safety criteria.

comparisons.objective: Candidate calibrates and locks an angular gripper; PR-2019 scrapes bonded char from a griddle into its grease tray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires precision tool seating and torque counterholding; PR-2019 requires maintaining a scraper-edge attitude, applying lateral force to break debris bonds, overlapping strokes, and controlling material flow.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate scores angle accuracy, hardware retention, cycles, drift, and release; PR-2019 scores debris mass transferred to the tray, cleanliness, scraper set-down, and penalties for off-griddle debris or gouging.
comparisons.reason: Surface scraping and debris containment test forceful planar tool use rather than coupled threaded adjustment and retained mechanism calibration; the scoring rubric is complete and quantitative.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts robot gripper hardware; PR-2062 keeps a machine-loader nest stocked during variable autonomous cycles.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coupled two-tool torque control; PR-2062 requires timed pick-place, precise nest seating, monitoring, and collision avoidance in shared workspace.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires retained angle across test cycles; PR-2062 awards credit for five blanks successfully supplied and carried away by the loader.
comparisons.reason: Both concern automation equipment, but they test configuration work versus reactive machine tending.

comparisons.objective: Candidate locks a gripper stop setting; PR-2082 clears a procedure tray while diverting a syringe to a sharps container.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses concentric tools and countertorque; PR-2082 requires hazard recognition, safe syringe extraction, precise disposal, and tray handling.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades retained angular setting; PR-2082 grades syringe/tray/forceps destinations with latched needle-touch and ordinary-waste hazards.
comparisons.reason: No adjustment, locknut preservation, or functional-cycle verification appears in PR-2082.

comparisons.objective: Candidate mechanically sets and locks a gripper stop; PR-2115 heats and solders a copper joint without burning flux.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests bimanual torque coupling; PR-2115 tests coordinated torch/filler placement, thermal timing, solder feeding, and safe cooling.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a locked angle retained through motion; PR-2115 requires sufficient solder, set joint, tools away, and no overheating or misdirected flame.
comparisons.reason: The shared use of two tools does not equate mechanical counterholding with heat-process control.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts industrial gripper hardware; PR-2127 extracts one cup from a gasket dispenser and stands it on a mat.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires driver/wrench seating and countertorque; PR-2127 requires a gentle pinch, straight compliant extraction, and stable placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades locking and repeated retained motion; PR-2127 grades exactly one undamaged cup removed, released upright, and positioned on the mat.
comparisons.reason: The compliant extraction and placement ability is meaningfully different from screw-and-locknut adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets a gripper opening stop; PR-2134 cinches and removes a loaded flexible bin liner.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests rigid concentric tool manipulation and countertorque; PR-2134 tests deformable closure, bimanual lifting, containment, and stable release.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires angular retention after cycles; PR-2134 requires a closed liner, retained contents, bin clearance, and stable released placement.
comparisons.reason: The record is a deformable containment task with no adjustable mechanical setting or functional verification.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a robot gripper stop; PR-2181 probes a burger through its side to take a central temperature reading.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses a driver and jam-nut wrench under reaction torque; PR-2181 stabilizes a patty with a turner while controlling probe entry angle and depth.
