comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires retained 90° motion over three cycles; PR-2181 requires a valid side entry, central one-second reading, limited patty motion, withdrawal, and tool replacement.
comparisons.reason: Bimanual stabilization is generic; probe insertion and measurement do not test setting preservation under locking torque.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop; PR-2259 loads a lancet into a lancing device, removes its tab, replaces the cap, and cocks the device.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires simultaneous driver-and-wrench countertorque; PR-2259 requires cap removal, small-part axial insertion, twist-off separation, snap fitting, spring cocking, and avoiding an exposed needle.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires retained angle over repeated gripper cycles; PR-2259 requires the lancet home, tab removed, cap snapped on, device cocked and laid down, with zero for needle proximity or device loss.
comparisons.reason: The lancet task is a sequential small-device assembly and sharps-safety procedure, not preservation of a continuous setting under concentric locknut reaction; its rubric states all material thresholds.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks a robot-gripper opening stop; PR-2260 packs a rolled poster into a mailing tube and seats an end cap at each end.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial driver and wrench manipulation with countertorque; PR-2260 requires long-object alignment and insertion, tube stabilization, and coaxial press-fitting of two caps.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a locked 90° setting, three repeatable cycles, retained nuts, and clearance; PR-2260 requires the roll sufficiently inside, one or both caps geometrically seated, hands off, stillness, real-world cap retention, and no poster damage.
comparisons.reason: Long-roll packing and friction-cap insertion do not test coupled adjustment locking or articulated setting retention; no material success-condition detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a gripper opening stop; PR-793 fits a rubber stopper at least 12 mm onto a glass tube while safely supporting the tube.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both use two hands against reaction, but the candidate controls two concentric threaded elements with separate tools to prevent locknut-induced setpoint rotation; PR-793 grips fragile glass close to the work while pushing and twisting an interference-fit stopper.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires angular accuracy, seated retained nuts, tool withdrawal, three repeatable cycles, and low drift; PR-793 requires insertion depth and release, with zero for unsupported working or glass damage.
comparisons.reason: Safe support during interference insertion does not subsume preservation of a calibrated threaded setting against its own locking torque and subsequent functional cycling; all versions expose the relevant safety and depth criteria.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts an industrial gripper opening stop; PR-2107 extends and locks a suitcase handle at full height.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires two-tool countertorque and regrasping; PR-2107 requires holding a case while maintaining a release-button press through a long telescoping stroke.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades a jam-nut-secured angle retained over cycles; PR-2107 grades both rails locked at 520 mm with the case stable and hands clear.
comparisons.reason: Although both end in a locked mechanical setting, the underlying tested abilities—countertorque adjustment versus button-held telescoping—are different.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks a gripper opening stop; PR-2108 aligns a flaring yoke and forms a copper-tube flare.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both use rotational hand tools, but the candidate couples a driver and thin-nut wrench to preserve an adjustment; PR-2108 sets tube height/yoke alignment, clamps, advances a forming cone through clutch release, and retracts it.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires retained 90° opening after repeated actuation; PR-2108 requires a geometrically good, sufficiently ironed flare with the cone retracted and hands clear.
comparisons.reason: PR-2108 tests irreversible alignment-dependent forming, not locknut counterholding or post-lock functional retention.

comparisons.objective: Candidate configures a robot gripper stop; PR-2200 loads a newsletter stack into a spring-raised autofolder feed table.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires concentric two-tool torque control; PR-2200 requires one hand to depress a sprung table while the other aligns and slides a broad stack to a stop.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades a locked angle and repeated retained motion; PR-2200 grades stack position, squareness, released clamping, machine stability, and clearance.
comparisons.reason: The shared need to resist a mechanism's restoring force is generic and supports different abilities and outcomes.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks a gripper opening stop, then verifies retained motion; PR-2241 levels a sand bed by pulling a screed board along rails.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial driver/wrench seating, countertorque, and preserving a screw setting while tightening a jam nut. PR-2241 requires bimanual board transport, rail contact, synchronized pulling, and controlled material redistribution.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades locked 90° opening accuracy, low drift across three cycles, hardware retention, and released clearance. PR-2241 grades a bridged pull, sand-depth flatness, lack of post-pass disturbance, board stowage, and release. Both include hands-off checks, but their functional outcomes differ.
comparisons.reason: The tested abilities are meaningfully different: coupled screw-and-locknut adjustment with retained articulated calibration versus guided screeding of bulk material. Both available spec versions were read and provide complete numeric rubrics; no material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Candidate calibrates and locks an existing gripper opening stop; PR-2243 removes a failed gas strut, installs a replacement, and checks the lid’s operation.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate centers two tools on a coupled screw/nut assembly and counterholds tightening reaction without shifting the setting. PR-2243 manipulates spring clips and ball sockets while supporting a hinged lid, then seats and retention-tests the replacement strut.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires target-angle accuracy, seated/retained nuts, three repeatable cycles, bounded drift, and hands-off clearance. PR-2243 requires removal and safe placement of the failed strut, correct two-end installation, lid hold-open and closure events, plus socket pull and lift tests.
comparisons.reason: Although both are bimanual maintenance tasks with functional verification, PR-2243 tests clip release, socket insertion, component replacement, and load support rather than countertorque-based calibration retention. Both available spec versions were read and provide complete numeric rubrics; no material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks a gripper opening limit; PR-2256 measures brake-rotor thickness with a handheld outside micrometer and preserves the reading after removal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires hex-driver and jam-nut-wrench countertorque; PR-2256 requires positioning a micrometer on a friction band, keeping it square, rocking for the minimum, and turning a ratchet to controlled measuring force.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a retained 90° gripper opening through three cycles; PR-2256 requires a reading within ±0.02 mm, two ratchet clicks, reading retention off the rotor, and released placement on the rest.
comparisons.reason: Although both retain a setting, PR-2256 tests metrological contact and reading preservation, not locking a mechanical adjustment against coupled fastening reaction or verifying articulated function; its rubric is numeric.

comparisons.objective: Install inner and outer brake pads and swing the caliper closed over them.
comparisons.physical_skill: Orient and insert two pads into tight retainers, seat their ears flush, then articulate a heavy caliper through millimeter clearances.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct pads flush on their respective sides with linings facing the disc, caliper closed within one degree, hands clear for two seconds.
comparisons.reason: Sequential tight-clearance insertion and caliper closure are meaningfully different from adjustment-screw regulation, locknut countertorque, and repeated opening verification.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a gripper opening stop; PR-892 loads a filled syringe into a pump, seats its flange, advances the driver gently, and in later versions closes the barrel clamp.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires concentric driver-and-wrench torque coordination; PR-892 requires syringe alignment and insertion, flange-slot seating, clamp articulation, and force-limited driver placement without moving the plunger.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires retained angle, hardware retention, repeated cycles, and released clearance; PR-892 requires a seated and clamped syringe, driver flush to the plunger, no plunger displacement, stillness, and a one-second hold.
comparisons.reason: Gentle medical-device loading and no-dose contact control do not test continuous stop adjustment, jam-nut reaction counterholding, or post-lock motion retention; the record's versions provide detailed thresholds.

comparisons.objective: Disinfect an IV connector, attach a syringe, and deliver a measured flush.
comparisons.physical_skill: Rub a small hub with sustained friction, align and seat a luer tip, and operate a syringe plunger without premature contamination.
comparisons.success_condition: Fifteen seconds of valid scrubbing precede syringe contact, at least 5 mL is expelled and at least 4.5 mL collected; early syringe contact permanently fails.
comparisons.reason: The task tests timed surface scrubbing, contamination avoidance, connector alignment, and fluid delivery rather than mechanical stop locking.

comparisons.objective: Prune a dead rose cane above a live bud, retain the cutting, and place it in a bin without harming the plant.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual secateur operation with precise cut placement and continuous control of a freed offcut.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct 3–15 mm stub, intact bud, cutting in bin, tool and hands released; green-cane cutting, dropping, or plant damage revokes credit.
comparisons.reason: The candidate tests concentric driver-and-wrench countertorque, retained stop calibration, and post-lock cycling, not cutting and controlling an offcut.

comparisons.objective: Load a caulking gun and apply a continuous silicone bead along a bath joint.
comparisons.physical_skill: Operate a release and plunger, seat a cartridge, meter the trigger, and guide a nozzle along a seam.
comparisons.success_condition: Credit follows cartridge loading and joint coverage; full credit requires at least 95% sealed with no gap over 2 mm and the gun released.
comparisons.reason: Its coupled actions load and dispense material, whereas the candidate preserves a screw-set angular stop while tightening a jam nut and verifies retention by cycling.

comparisons.objective: Candidate configures a robot gripper stop; PR-1530 finishes painting a partially coated panel without excessive overlap.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial driver/wrench manipulation; PR-1530 requires visual coverage planning and controlled roller contact, orientation, and strokes.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires mechanical lock retention over cycles; PR-1530 scores bare-cell coverage, repaint waste, and avoidance of table contamination.
comparisons.reason: Surface coverage control is unrelated to calibrated screw-and-jam-nut locking.

comparisons.objective: Move a tissue-roll stub to the reserve spindle, install a new primary roll, set the changeover shutter, and close the dispenser.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold release buttons while extracting and seating large cores, then manipulate a shutter and sprung cover.
comparisons.success_condition: Credit requires correctly engaged rolls in their assigned hubs, a latched cover, correct shutter position, and released hands; misassignment and unsafe closure fail.
comparisons.reason: This tests release-controlled core transfer and dispenser sequencing, not preserving an adjustable screw setting against jam-nut reaction or validating repeated motion.

comparisons.objective: Seat four wired connector modules in a sprung hinged frame and close it until latched.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated tight-clearance insertion of adjacent modules followed by closure without dislodging them.
comparisons.success_condition: Full credit requires all four modules seated within millimetre tolerances, frame clicked shut, hands clear, and a one-second hold; dropped or crushed modules fail.
comparisons.reason: Multi-part insertion and sprung-frame latching are meaningfully different from two-tool countertorque calibration and hands-off cycle retention.

comparisons.objective: Reset tongue-and-groove pliers from the narrowest to the widest groove and leave them locked.
comparisons.physical_skill: Open past a release angle, translate a slip joint along its slot, then close it into a discrete groove.
comparisons.success_condition: Full credit requires groove 5 locked, pliers flat and still, and hands clear for one second; intermediate grooves receive partial credit.
comparisons.reason: Although both change and retain an opening, this record tests release-angle-gated sliding into a discrete groove, while the candidate tests continuous screw adjustment preserved through jam-nut countertorque and three functional cycles.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts a gripper opening stop; PR-2013 squares a racked two-rail gantry against paired end stops.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both are robot-hardware tasks with bimanual force coordination, but the candidate counterholds concentric screw/nut tools while PR-2013 advances both beam ends together to avoid rail binding.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a locked target angle retained through three cycles; PR-2013 requires both carriage gaps at most 0.05 mm, rail seating, stillness, and release.
comparisons.reason: PR-2013 tests synchronized linear squaring; it has no adjustable fastener, locking reaction, or functional retention cycle.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks gripper hardware; PR-2133 measures tyre tread depth with a friction-held pen gauge.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coupled rotational tools and countertorque; PR-2133 requires placing a probe on a groove floor while seating a foot across ribs, then withdrawing without changing the reading.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades retained angular adjustment after cycles; PR-2133 grades a reading within 1/32 inch after valid seating and return of the gauge to its rest.
comparisons.reason: Both preserve a setting during withdrawal in a broad sense, but only the candidate tests locknut-induced disturbance and retained articulated motion.

comparisons.objective: Candidate configures a gripper opening stop; PR-2198 divides a dough log into four portions at marked locations.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests coaxial driver/wrench torque control; PR-2198 tests vertical scraper alignment, controlled chopping through compliant material, and avoiding drag or incomplete cuts.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a locked 90° opening retained over three cycles; PR-2198 requires three complete cuts at marks, four ordered pieces, no creases or loss, tools down, and hands clear.
comparisons.reason: The cutting and portioning outcome is unrelated to adjustable-stop locking and cycle verification.

comparisons.objective: Shave a manikin's cheek and jaw while holding the cheek skin taut and avoiding sensitive features.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual skin tensioning plus force-limited curved-surface following with an electric shaver.
comparisons.success_condition: At least 95% coverage and shaver returned, released, and still; excessive force, sensitive-feature contact, head displacement, or dropping latches zero.
comparisons.reason: Force-controlled surface coverage on compliant anatomy is unrelated to coaxial adjustment, jam-nut counterholding, and retained articulated motion.

comparisons.objective: Move a hot iron to the requested area and leave it heel-standing without soleplate contact, versus adjusting and locking a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Safe grasping, transport, and reorientation of an iron differs from coaxial tool seating, jam-nut countertorque, and articulated verification.
comparisons.success_condition: The iron task requires placement in the right-hand zone, heel stability, and no hazardous contact; it does not require a retained mechanical adjustment.
comparisons.reason: The task tests hazard-aware reorientation and placement, not setting and locking an adjustable mechanism.

comparisons.objective: Seal, shake, open, and safely leave a mixed drink in a Boston shaker.
comparisons.physical_skill: Create a press-fit seal, perform bimanual reciprocating motion that moves ice end to end, break the seal, and control spill.
comparisons.success_condition: Required mixing or shake cycles, minimal loss, shaker reopened, and large tin upright; tipping while unsealed or losing ice fails.
comparisons.reason: Both use two-handed reaction management, but shaker sealing, dynamic mixing, and spill control do not test precision screw setting or locknut retention.

comparisons.objective: Measure a standing pin with a handheld digital caliper and return the caliper to its rest.
comparisons.physical_skill: Align jaws squarely, close them with very low force, stabilize a reading, and release the instrument.
comparisons.success_condition: Accuracy, angular alignment, jaw force, contact on both jaws, final placement, clearance, and stillness determine credit.
comparisons.reason: Both involve precision, but caliper metrology tests gentle bilateral contact and reading accuracy, not mechanically locking a setting against tightening torque and cycling it.

comparisons.objective: Fully unfold a passive laptop stand and seat both support rods in its highest slots inside a marked area.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coordinate a scissor linkage and insert two support rods into separate detents.
comparisons.success_condition: Independent credit covers full spread and each rod; full credit additionally requires both rails supported, outline inside the rectangle, and release.
comparisons.reason: This is articulated unfolding and dual rod seating; it has no threaded adjustment, coupled locknut reaction, or repeated-motion retention test. The rubric does not numerically define “full spread” or gripper-clear distance, but that omission does not create plausible overlap.

comparisons.objective: Fit a spring tension rod level between cupboard walls at a marked height so it supports itself.
comparisons.physical_skill: Compress and align a telescoping sprung rod while establishing frictional contact at both ends.
comparisons.success_condition: The released rod must press both walls, remain still and clear of the table, meet height/level/square limits, and hold full conditions for four seconds.
comparisons.reason: Spring compression and frictional placement between walls do not test tool-mediated stop calibration, jam-nut countertorque, or functional cycling.

comparisons.objective: Assemble and mesh three gears on assigned shafts, versus set and lock an angular-gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-893 requires shaft insertion and tooth-phase discovery by contact; the candidate requires screw adjustment, jam-nut counterholding, and tool regrasping.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-893 requires three seated, meshed, still gears with arms clear; the candidate requires angle accuracy, locking, low drift, and repeated articulated motion.
comparisons.reason: Gear phasing and multi-part insertion are meaningfully different from adjustment retention under locknut torque.

comparisons.objective: Turn and place a brad nailer into its case without pointing it at a coworker or touching the trigger.
comparisons.physical_skill: Safety-constrained rigid-tool reorientation, possibly with a bimanual handoff.
comparisons.success_condition: Any unsafe pointing or finger-trigger proximity causes zero; credit otherwise depends on final placement, release, and stillness.
comparisons.reason: Its tested ability is hazard-aware reorientation along a safe path, unrelated to coupled threaded adjustment and retention verification.

comparisons.objective: Remove a jammed card from a printer without tearing it, put it down, and resume printing.
comparisons.physical_skill: Apply balanced bimanual extraction forces at both card edges, then operate a button.
comparisons.success_condition: Credit tracks extraction and placement; seam shear of 1.5 mm causes irrevocable zero, and full credit requires the OK press, clearance, and one-second stillness.
comparisons.reason: Balanced extraction of a fragile sheet tests symmetric pulling and tear avoidance, not countertorque between concentric tools or preservation of a calibrated stop.

comparisons.objective: Set a telescoping gauge to a bore diameter and leave it retained on a stand, versus set a gripper opening stop and lock it.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1880 uses bore contact, gauge rocking, plunger locking, extraction, and placement; the candidate uses coaxial driver/wrench seating and countertorque against jam-nut reaction.
comparisons.success_condition: Both retain a calibrated setting after release, but PR-1880 requires a span within 0.10 mm and stand placement, while the candidate requires nut seating and repeated gripper actuation with limited drift.
comparisons.reason: Setting retention is shared, but contact metrology and withdrawing a telescoping gauge test a different physical ability from locking an adjustment screw under coupled torque.

comparisons.objective: Place a shackle around a towing lug and screw its pin fully home, versus adjust and lock a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1886 requires multi-hole alignment, pin insertion, thread starting, and repeated regrasping; the candidate requires preserving a continuous screw setting while tightening its jam nut.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1886 requires the pin through all three holes, collar seated, and hand-tight; it does not require retention of a calibrated adjustment or functional cycling.
comparisons.reason: Threading is shared only as a generic primitive; the shackle task tests aligned assembly rather than counterheld adjustment locking.

comparisons.objective: Seat and tighten a positive battery cable clamp on its tapered post with correct cable orientation.
comparisons.physical_skill: Align a spring-loaded clamp, seat it fully, and torque one pinch nut with a wrench.
comparisons.success_condition: Full credit requires seating, 5–7 N·m nut torque, lug alignment, safe wrench placement, hand clearance, and stillness; high, crooked, misplaced, or moved assemblies fail.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest threaded-tool record, but it tightens one clamp nut to a torque after seating; the candidate uniquely requires simultaneous driver counterholding to preserve a continuous stop setting and repeated articulated-cycle retention.

comparisons.objective: Transfer and quarter-turn-lock an air-line gladhand to the correct trailer connector, versus set and jam-lock a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1960 requires hose handling, face alignment, seal compression, and bayonet rotation; the candidate requires two-tool screw/nut countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1960 requires the correct connector, small plate gap, lock-stop angle, pull retention, and release; the candidate requires angular-setting accuracy and cycle repeatability.
comparisons.reason: Connector mating and bayonet locking are different from preserving an adjustable stop while tightening a jam nut.

comparisons.objective: Align and press two boards together over three dowels, versus adjust and lock a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2003 requires bimanual multi-axis insertion and even pressing across three pins; the candidate requires rotational tool seating and countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2003 scores insertion depth, seam gaps, flush edges, flatness, release, and stillness; the candidate scores retained angular calibration and cycles.
comparisons.reason: Multi-dowel alignment and insertion are unrelated to adjustable-stop locking.

comparisons.objective: Add a personal padlock through a free group-lockout hasp hole without disturbing a coworker’s lock or enabling the switch.
comparisons.physical_skill: Align and insert a shackle through two hasp jaws, close its latch, and avoid disturbing an existing safety assembly.
comparisons.success_condition: Full credit requires the closed lock to withstand hasp-pry and handle-on tests after release; moving the coworker’s lock or opening/turning the mechanism early causes irrevocable zero.
comparisons.reason: Shackle insertion and safety interlocking do not involve threaded calibration, reaction counterholding, or verification of a retained angular stop.

comparisons.objective: Water soil while holding a springy leaf aside and avoiding wet leaves, versus adjust and lock a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1272 requires simultaneous obstruction control and controlled pouring; the candidate requires coaxial fastener manipulation and countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1272 scores delivered water, leaf contamination, restored leaf/jug positions, and arm clearance; the candidate scores mechanical setting and retained function.
comparisons.reason: Bimanual coordination is generic; liquid delivery around an obstruction is a different tested ability.

comparisons.objective: Cut a cable tie from a bundle without damaging insulation, versus set and lock a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1441 stabilizes a rolling bundle while precisely positioning and closing flush cutters; the candidate counterholds a screw while tightening a jam nut.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1441 requires complete tie removal, no cable nick, tool return, and bundle stability; the candidate requires retained angle and repeated cycles.
comparisons.reason: Damage-avoiding cutting is meaningfully different from adjustment and locknut control.

comparisons.objective: Send a loaded tote down a roller conveyor to a distant station without a damaging impact.
comparisons.physical_skill: Impart a calibrated release velocity while keeping a loose bottle stable and respecting a no-reach zone.
comparisons.success_condition: Tote stops in the target zone with the bottle upright and low impact speed; excessive impact, tipping, lifting, or reaching into the forbidden area fails.
comparisons.reason: This tests momentum estimation and controlled release, not tool alignment, countertorque, locking, or mechanism calibration.

comparisons.objective: Push a shower-valve cartridge fully home against O-ring resistance and install its U-shaped retaining clip.
comparisons.physical_skill: Maintain axial force and angular alignment with one hand while inserting a close-clearance clip with the other.
comparisons.success_condition: Full credit requires the cartridge flush and square, clip fully seated, retention under a 20 N pull, hands clear, and a one-second hold; a dropped clip fails.
comparisons.reason: It shares genuine bimanual stabilization, but tests simultaneous press-and-clip insertion against spring-back, not two-tool screw/nut countertorque, target-angle preservation, and repeated cycling.

comparisons.objective: Flex a 3D-printer build plate to release a printed part without kinking it, versus adjust and lock a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1949 requires symmetric controlled elastic bending and part capture; the candidate requires rigid tool seating, turning, and countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1949 requires part release into a bin, plate restoration, curvature safety, stillness, and clearance; the candidate requires retained angle and functional cycles.
comparisons.reason: Controlled elastic flexure and release are unrelated to threaded adjustment locking.

comparisons.objective: Fit a separate key and keyed pulley onto a freely rotating shaft, versus set and lock a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2037 counterholds a shaft while placing a key, phase-aligning a pulley keyway, and sliding the pulley home; the candidate counterholds an adjustment screw while tightening its concentric jam nut.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2037 requires key seating, pulley insertion to the shoulder, release, and one-second stillness; the candidate requires nut locking and repeated retained-angle cycles.
comparisons.reason: Counterholding is shared, but keyed multi-part alignment and insertion are meaningfully different from preserving a continuous setting under tightening torque; no task.json spec was available, but the PR body provides the full staged rubric.

comparisons.objective: Spin wet lettuce in a hand-crank salad spinner at drying speed while keeping the loose lid and bowl stable.
comparisons.physical_skill: Continuously crank a moving knob while the other hand restrains a reaction-loaded bowl and lid.
comparisons.success_condition: Credit depends on basket speed above 300 rpm for specified durations and final crank release; excessive base motion, tilt, or lid displacement causes zero.
comparisons.reason: Bimanual reaction restraint is generic overlap only; sustained cranking and lid stability do not test precision stop adjustment, jam-nut locking, or drift after cycles.

comparisons.objective: Mount and align a dogbone specimen in two tensile-tester wedge grips at a specified gauge length, versus set and lock a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2186 requires two-ended specimen insertion, spring-lever operation, straightening, and crosshead jogging; the candidate requires coaxial screw/nut tool coordination and countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2186 scores independent tab seating, lever closure, end clearances, 115 mm jaw spacing, alignment, clearance, and a three-second hold; the candidate requires retained stop angle and repeated gripper cycles.
comparisons.reason: Precision specimen fixturing in two clamps tests distributed insertion and alignment, not preservation of a threaded adjustment against locknut reaction.

comparisons.objective: Set and lock a gripper opening stop versus function-test an emergency stop, reset, and separate restart control.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires concentric driver-and-wrench countertorque that preserves an angular setting; this task requires pushing, twisting, and pressing separate machine controls.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks retained 90° opening across three released cycles; this task checks latched stopping, non-restart after release, deliberate restart, and final clearance.
comparisons.reason: Functional verification is shared only generically; the adjusted locknut mechanism and tested manipulation ability are different.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts a gripper’s threaded opening stop, locks the setting, and verifies retained motion; PR 2250 assembles a laryngoscope blade onto a hinge bar and opens it into a lit detent.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires simultaneous hex-driver counterholding and thin-jam-nut tightening so lock torque does not disturb the stop, followed by tool withdrawal and actuation. PR 2250 requires slot-to-bar hook insertion, hinged swinging with regrasping, and detent engagement; it does not test coupled threaded adjustment or countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate scores target opening accuracy, seated/retained nuts, three repeatable cycles, limited stop drift, and released clearance. PR 2250 scores blade hook depth/alignment, at least 45° swing, 90° lit-detent engagement, tray placement, release, and one-second stillness, with off-table loss scoring zero. Both available PR 2250 spec versions agree; no material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: The shared ideas of articulated motion, final release, and functional checking are generic. The candidate’s defining tested ability is preserving a calibrated threaded stop while locking it against reaction torque and proving retention across cycles, whereas PR 2250 tests hook-on assembly and detent latching of two initially separate parts.

comparisons.objective: Raise a care-bed side rail until its spring latch catches.
comparisons.physical_skill: Swing a gravity-loaded rail through an arc and push a ramped latch tooth into its keeper before releasing.
comparisons.success_condition: Rail remains at the upright position with the latch caught and hands clear for one second; raising then dropping the rail permanently fails.
comparisons.reason: A single contact-driven latch operation differs from selecting an opening angle, preserving it during jam-nut tightening, and confirming it through repeated cycles.

comparisons.objective: Set and lock a gripper stop versus relocate a hot iron and leave it safely standing on its heel.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses coaxial tool seating and coupled screw/nut counterholding; the iron task requires grasping, carrying, reorienting, and balancing a bulky tool.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires locked angle retention through repeated actuation; the iron task requires stable heel placement in the right-hand mat region without an unsafe face-down dwell.
comparisons.reason: The objects, manipulation mechanics, and retained outcome are unrelated beyond generic safe release.

comparisons.objective: Calibrate and lock a gripper opening limit versus orient and insert a battery, then thread a flashlight tail cap.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both involve rotation while another object is stabilized, but the candidate requires simultaneous driver counterholding against a jam nut; the flashlight requires close-fit insertion and cap thread engagement.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate scores preserved 90° adjustment and repeated-cycle drift; the flashlight scores correct battery polarity and a cap seated after at least 300° of threading.
comparisons.reason: Generic bimanual screwing overlaps, but coupled adjustment preservation and post-lock functional cycling test a meaningfully different ability.

comparisons.objective: Adjust and lock an articulated gripper stop versus depanel a scored circuit board and tray the freed board.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses two concentric tools to regulate screw and jam-nut rotation; depaneling registers a score line, braces a frame, and applies controlled downward bending to fracture it.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires retained opening across cycles; depaneling requires a valid edge-supported downward break, intact placement in a tray, and safe scrap placement.
comparisons.reason: Although both use bimanual reaction control, one preserves a calibrated threaded setting and the other produces controlled fracture.

comparisons.objective: Set and lock a gripper opening stop versus load two forceps open into a sterilizer basket.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires tool-mediated countertorque and later fixture actuation; forceps handling requires opening friction hinges, carrying articulated tools, and placing them flat without stacking.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks locked angular repeatability; forceps scoring checks both instruments released, flat, inside the basket, and at least 15° open.
comparisons.reason: Articulated motion is common, but the tested abilities and end states are different.

comparisons.objective: Shake a separatory funnel to mix two layers, periodically vent it safely, and return it to its support.
comparisons.physical_skill: Control a stoppered vessel during vigorous oscillation while reorienting and operating a stopcock to manage pressure.
comparisons.success_condition: Stroke count and safe venting determine credit; overpressure, unsafe valve orientation, or loss of contents fails, while full credit requires 12 strokes and stable released placement.
comparisons.reason: The task tests hazardous vessel shaking and periodic pressure relief, not calibrated threaded adjustment, coupled locking, or retained articulated motion.

comparisons.objective: Set and lock a robot-gripper opening limit versus measure a sprung training doll on an infantometer.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate counterholds a screw during jam-nut tightening; the infantometer task holds four sprung leg joints straight while sliding a footboard to both soles.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks locked 90° return over cycles; the infantometer checks a valid crown-to-footboard measurement retained after both arms release.
comparisons.reason: Both resist a physical restoring reaction, but the mechanisms, manipulation, and observable outcomes differ materially.

comparisons.objective: Remove a binder clip from invoices and feed the paper stack into a shredder safely.
comparisons.physical_skill: Support a thin stack, open and remove a sprung clip, align the stack edge-on with a narrow feed slot, and manage the removed clip.
comparisons.success_condition: Paper shredded and clip safely released away from the shredder, with hands clear; feeding the clip, entering the slot with fingers, or dropping material fails.
comparisons.reason: Spring-clip removal and hazardous slot feeding test different manipulation and outcomes from gripper-stop adjustment and countertorque locking.

comparisons.objective: Adjust and lock a gripper stop versus mount a filled malt cup on a spindle mixer to activate it without spilling.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial tool engagement and countertorque; mixer mounting requires tipping a heavy cup around a fixed spindle, threading its rim behind a guide, and seating it on a narrow step.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks angle retention and repeated actuation; mixer scoring checks spindle containment, run-step seating, switch-pin activation, release, stability, and no excessive tilt.
comparisons.reason: Machine functional verification appears in both, but the physical ability is calibrated locking versus constrained vessel mounting.

comparisons.objective: Set and lock a gripper opening stop versus install an oversized cabinet shelf through a narrower face-frame opening.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses small-tool seating and coupled rotational force control; shelf installation requires bimanual roll-to-fit transport, in-cavity leveling, and four-point support placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a locked angle that survives cycling; shelf success requires released contact on all four pins, level and square placement, and a specified back gap.
comparisons.reason: The shelf task tests constrained large-object reorientation and support placement, not threaded adjustment retention.

comparisons.objective: Adjust and lock a robot-gripper stop versus clean an SC ferrule and latch the connector into a panel adapter.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses a driver and wrench on coupled hardware; the fibre task requires a one-way contact wipe followed by contamination-free tight insertion and latch engagement.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks nut retention and repeatable jaw angle; fibre scoring checks a valid wipe before insertion, no prohibited ferrule contact, and final connector latch/release.
comparisons.reason: Both are AI-hardware service tasks, but industrial labels and generic precision do not erase the different tested abilities.

comparisons.objective: Cut marked copper tubing without denting or spiraling the cut; candidate instead sets and locks a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeatedly feed and orbit a tubing cutter with handoffs; no jam-nut counterholding that preserves an angular setting.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires controlled groove depth, completed cut, roundness, mark accuracy, and release; candidate requires retained 90° opening across three cycles.
comparisons.reason: Both use tools and rotational control, but the tested mechanisms and outcomes—progressive cutting versus lock-preserved stop adjustment—are meaningfully different.

comparisons.objective: Mix flour and liquid into dough while stabilizing a loose bowl; candidate adjusts and locks a mechanical gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stabilize a vessel while sweeping a spoon through granular ingredients; no coaxial driver/wrench coupling or setting retention.
comparisons.success_condition: Scores mixed-flour share while penalizing tipping and material loss; candidate scores opening angle, locked retention, cycling, and clearance.
comparisons.reason: Shared bimanual stabilization is generic; mixing distributed material does not test countertorque locking of an adjustable stop.

comparisons.objective: Set and lock a mechanical opening stop versus perform a two-hand musical passage with specified notes, timing, and dynamics.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires sustained tool seating and rotational counterforce; keyboard playing requires coordinated key timing, simultaneous notes, differential strike velocities, and releases.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks retained angle and hardware state after cycling; keyboard success checks note order, onset synchronization, velocity separation, tempo regularity, and final key/hand clearance.
comparisons.reason: No meaningful objective, mechanism, or outcome overlap exists.

comparisons.objective: Adjust and lock a robot-gripper stop versus transport four visually identical cups with hidden, different payloads.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires countertorque between a hex driver and wrench; cup handling requires payload-sensitive grip-force adaptation that avoids slip and panel buckling.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks locked angle retention; cup scoring awards each upright released placement only after a valid side-wall lift without crushing, dropping, or excessive tilt.
comparisons.reason: Force control is shared only at a broad level; adaptive grasp-force inference is different from preserving a threaded setting.

comparisons.objective: Set and lock a gripper opening limit versus make space in a stocked shelf row and insert a new carton in order.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses precision coupled rotation with two tools; stocking requires sliding or relocating multiple upright cartons and placing another into a constrained gap.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks angular tolerance, lock retention, and repeated motion; stocking checks ordered upright placement of all five cartons, separation, stillness, and gripper clearance.
comparisons.reason: This is constrained rearrangement rather than mechanical calibration or locking.

comparisons.objective: Set and lock a robot-gripper stop versus clear a washbasin blockage with a plunger.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate needs coaxial tool seating and countertorque; plunging needs cup-seal formation, overflow control, and pressure strokes that dislodge a wet obstruction.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks retained opening after three cycles; basin scoring checks drained volume, a persistently clear bore, limited leakage, intact plumbing, and final plunger clearance.
comparisons.reason: Both verify a maintained functional outcome, but the pressure-seal manipulation and hydraulic result are unrelated to threaded stop locking.

comparisons.objective: Calibrate and lock a gripper stop versus empty four concentrate bottles while timing closure of a running tank inlet.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses simultaneous precision countertorque; batching requires repeated liquid pours, level monitoring, and quarter-turn valve manipulation under a changing fill state.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks a retained mechanical angle; all eight batching specifications require emptied bottles, a shut valve, final level near the fill line, and no overflow, spill, bottle loss, or tank movement.
comparisons.reason: The task tests coordinated batching and flow termination, not preservation of an adjustable threaded stop.

comparisons.objective: Set and lock a robot-gripper opening stop versus recover an overhanging cube inward before lifting it onto a pedestal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires driver/wrench countertorque and functional cycling; recovery requires support-aware pushing, grasping, sequencing, and stable placement near a real table edge.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks nut retention and repeated angle return; the available PR body specifies inward recovery, lift only after recovery, pedestal placement, and irreversible edge, tilt, fall, or premature-lift failures.
comparisons.reason: No task.json or versioned rubric is available in the record, but the complete PR body supplies enough concrete milestones and failures to establish a different tested ability.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets a gripper opening stop, locks the adjustment, and verifies retained motion; PR-2188 installs a case fan into a tool-less bracket.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial driver seating plus wrench countertorque on a coupled screw/jam nut; PR-2188 requires square fan alignment, guided lowering, and pressing through two spring latches.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades 90° adjustment accuracy, seated/retained nuts, three repeatable cycles, drift, and tool clearance; PR-2188 grades fan insertion, both hooks snapped over it, release, and one-second stability.
comparisons.reason: Snap-fitting a separate fan does not test preserving an adjustable setting during locknut reaction or verifying that setting through repeated articulated cycles; no material comparison rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Set and lock a gripper stop versus snap a specimen swab at its breakpoint while retaining the tip in a loose transport tube.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate counterholds concentric screw and nut tooling; the swab task braces a very light tube while bending a thin shaft to controlled fracture, then disposes of the handle.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks locked angle retention through cycles; swab scoring requires a valid in-tube break, no spill or tip escape, handle in the waste cup, upright tube, rest, and gripper clearance.
comparisons.reason: Bimanual reaction control is shared, but calibrated locking and controlled fracture are meaningfully different abilities.

comparisons.objective: Lock out an AC pull-out disconnect by reversing its pull-out block and securing the cover with a padlock.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a hinged cover, extract and invert a keyed block, reinsert it, and thread and latch a padlock.
comparisons.success_condition: The correct disconnect is OFF, its cover is shut and withstands a pull test while padlocked, and the neighboring disconnect remains untouched.
comparisons.reason: Its core ability is multi-stage extraction, inversion, insertion, and shackle latching rather than preserving a calibrated stop under tightening reaction.

comparisons.objective: Open a folding-table leg, lock its brace ring over the knee, and prove the lock under side load.
comparisons.physical_skill: Articulate a leg and four-bar brace, slide a separate ring over the brace joint, withdraw, and withstand a load test.
comparisons.success_condition: Leg upright, ring at least 12 mm past the knee pin, hands clear, and no more than 3 degrees folding under the 6 N load test.
comparisons.reason: Both tasks lock an adjustment and verify retention, but this record tests sliding a brace ring over an articulated knee; it lacks precision screw adjustment and simultaneous screw/nut countertorque.

comparisons.objective: Measure subfloor flatness with a straightedge and wedge, then report PASS or FAIL.
comparisons.physical_skill: Place a long reference tool, probe for the deepest gap with a tapered gauge, read the measurement, and classify it.
comparisons.success_condition: The wedge reads the deepest trough within 0.3 mm under a correctly placed straightedge and the puck is in the correct decision pocket.
comparisons.reason: This is precision inspection and reporting with a wedge gauge, with no threaded adjustment, locknut countertorque, or functional cycling.

comparisons.objective: Safely move a carton to a shelf after stabilizing a glazed picture leaning on it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Recognize a support dependency, relocate a fragile frame without dropping it, and then transfer the carton.
comparisons.success_condition: The picture is stably set down without a recorded fall and the carton is released upright on the shelf.
comparisons.reason: It tests dependency-aware fragile-object handling and placement, not coupled tool use on an adjustable mechanism.

comparisons.objective: Hot-swap a failed server power supply without disturbing the live redundant supply.
comparisons.physical_skill: Squeeze a release tab while pulling a long module, align a replacement in rails, overcome connector force, and latch it.
comparisons.success_condition: The failed PSU is removed, the spare is fully seated and latched for one second, and the live PSU never moves over 5 mm.
comparisons.reason: Although industrial and retention-sensitive, it tests constrained module extraction/insertion and latch engagement rather than setting-and-locking a screw with countertorque.

comparisons.objective: Break a basin stopper's suction seal and place the stopper in a soap dish.
comparisons.physical_skill: Reach under a faucet obstruction, grasp a small knob, resist a sudden seal release, and transfer the stopper.
comparisons.success_condition: The seal is broken and the stopper is released, still, and clear of both grippers in the soap dish.
comparisons.reason: This is constrained pulling and post-release transport, not angular adjustment, jam-nut locking, or retained-motion verification.

comparisons.objective: Install a tempered-glass phone protector using its close-fitting alignment tray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Lower a tray square over a phone, press the glass to adhere it, and remove the tray without shifting the glass.
comparisons.success_condition: The glass is flat and within 1.5 mm at every corner, with the empty tray removed and hands clear for one second.
comparisons.reason: It tests planar alignment, adhesion activation, and fixture removal rather than reaction-sensitive threaded locking.

comparisons.objective: Level a floor sleeper by inserting a tapered shim under its low end.
comparisons.physical_skill: Lift a loaded member, start and advance a shim by a controlled amount, and use a bubble level as feedback.
comparisons.success_condition: The sleeper is supported with full shim bearing and within 1 mm end-to-end level, with the level left on and hands clear.
comparisons.reason: Both tasks adjust to a measured target, but this uses translational wedge insertion under load and has no screw/nut counterholding or cycle-retention test.

comparisons.objective: Start a loose nail at a marked point and hammer it flush into a board.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a tiny nail while striking it, withdraw the supporting hand safely, deliver repeated aligned impacts, and regrasp the hammer.
comparisons.success_condition: The nail is flush, upright, and on the mark; the hammer is released; bent nails or striking the supporting gripper invalidate the run.
comparisons.reason: Its defining ability is coordinated impact tool use and hand withdrawal, not continuous torque balance during adjustment and locking.

comparisons.objective: Remove the internal burr from a cut copper tube without over-chamfering it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold the tube against cutting torque, coaxially seat a reamer, make controlled rotary strokes, and repeatedly regrasp it.
comparisons.success_condition: Every bore sector receives the required passes without excessive chamfer, and the tube and reamer are returned and released.
comparisons.reason: It shares coaxial tool seating, regrasping, and reaction torque, but tests controlled material removal while holding a workpiece rather than preserving a screw setting during jam-nut lock and subsequent actuation.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks an assembled gripper’s opening stop; PR-2251 installs and electrically engages a T8 tube in two rotor lampholders.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests concentric two-tool screw/nut counterholding and later lever actuation; PR-2251 tests bimanual support of a long fragile tube, simultaneous dual-end pin insertion, and coordinated quarter-turn rotation.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a retained 90° opening across three cycles with limited drift, retained nuts, and withdrawn tools; PR-2251 requires both pin pairs inserted, both rotors at their 90° stops, illumination, release, and one-second stillness.
comparisons.reason: Although both involve angular regulation and functional verification, dual-end lamp insertion and rotation do not exercise coupled screw-and-locknut adjustment under countertorque; no material comparison rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Use a tweezer puller to remove the middle blade fuse and deposit it in a tray without disturbing its neighbors.
comparisons.physical_skill: Orient a sprung puller crosswise, insert its jaws between adjacent fuses, squeeze, extract vertically, release, and set down the tool.
comparisons.success_condition: Target fuse rests in the tray, puller is open and released, and both are still and clear; moving neighboring fuses or losing the fuse or puller fails.
comparisons.reason: Crowded extraction with a spring tool is a different tested ability from concentric screw-and-locknut manipulation and retained-angle verification.

comparisons.objective: Seat a strain-wave flexspline unit into a robot-joint housing with its teeth meshed.
comparisons.physical_skill: Align two axes, rotate to tooth phase while applying insertion force, avoid cocking, and release after seating.
comparisons.success_condition: The collar is within 0.5 mm of the housing face, teeth are meshed, alignment tolerances hold, and the unit remains still after release.
comparisons.reason: This robot-assembly task tests turn-to-mesh precision insertion, not two-tool threaded adjustment, countertorque locking, or repeated motion retention.

comparisons.objective: Replace the blown fuse in the named DIN-rail holder with the correctly rated spare and relatch the carrier.
comparisons.physical_skill: Select the correct part, open a small hinged carrier, remove and insert cartridge fuses, close the latch, and avoid adjacent holders.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct KTK-6 fuse seated in F2, carrier shut and passing a 4 N pull check, old fuse in the tray; opening neighbors or installing KTK-10 latches zero.
comparisons.reason: Part selection, cartridge replacement, and carrier relatching differ from setting a continuous mechanical angle, counterholding a screw during jam-nut tightening, and repeated actuation checks.

comparisons.objective: Fasten a screw through an upright plate into a coupling nut held on the far side.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually align separate screw and nut, hold the nut against rotation, catch the thread, and turn the screw until snug.
comparisons.success_condition: The screw passes through the plate, engages for at least 1.5 turns, and leaves both head and nut snug after release.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest generic fastening primitive, but it creates a new screw-nut joint to a snug endpoint; the candidate preserves an existing adjustable stop against jam-nut reaction and must prove its setting through repeated actuation.

comparisons.objective: Drive a curved suture needle through a practice pad along its arc and hand it to the other gripper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Rotate a curved needle about its center, avoid lateral tissue loading, grasp the emerging section, and execute a controlled handoff.
comparisons.success_condition: The needle traverses both slots without tearing or pad contact, the second hand holds it, and the first releases it while it remains threaded.
comparisons.reason: This tests curved-path insertion and in-place handoff, unrelated to threaded adjustment, counterholding, and lock retention.

comparisons.objective: Extend a loose paint-roller pole to a marked length, relock its internal twist cam, and prove load retention; the candidate instead sets a gripper opening-stop screw, locks its jam nut without disturbing the setting, and cycles the gripper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both require bimanual counter-rotation and retention, but PR-1855 counter-twists and axially slides two tubes; the candidate requires coaxial driver/wrench seating and countertorque during locknut tightening.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1855 requires 93–95 cm length and under 2 mm shortening during a 50 N push; the candidate requires a retained 90° opening, limited drift, three repeated cycles, retained nuts, and released clearance.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest record, but preserving a threaded adjustment while tightening its concentric jam nut and then verifying articulated cycles is meaningfully different from setting and load-testing a telescoping cam lock.

comparisons.objective: Use a plumb bob to transfer a shelf-hole position onto a worktop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Damp a pendulum by touch, release it without re-excitation, and mark accurately in a narrow clearance while it hangs freely.
comparisons.success_condition: All pencil marks are made while the bob is free and still and lie within 3 mm of plumb, with the pencil lifted afterward.
comparisons.reason: Its defining ability is dynamic pendulum damping followed by precision marking, not tool-mediated mechanical adjustment and locking.

comparisons.objective: Fit a smartphone into a hybrid case in the correct orientation and snap all corners under the lip.
comparisons.physical_skill: Orient a thin fragile object, align an asymmetric camera feature, and sequentially press corners through compliant latches.
comparisons.success_condition: All four corners are seated under the lip with the phone correctly oriented and the case flat, released, and still.
comparisons.reason: This is compliant snap-fit insertion with orientation constraints, not threaded countertorque or functional setting verification.

comparisons.objective: Mark a banknote with a counterfeit pen while pinning it, then sort it according to the mark.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stabilize an extremely light sheet against pen drag, draw a controlled stroke, return the pen, and slide the note without lifting it.
comparisons.success_condition: A valid pinned stroke is made, the pen is returned, and the note is released flat on the correct result mat without prohibited ink or smearing.
comparisons.reason: It tests sheet stabilization during marking and result-based sorting rather than coupled mechanical adjustment and locking.

comparisons.objective: Connect a mop frame's swiveling socket to its handle until the spring button clicks.
comparisons.physical_skill: Counterpose an articulated socket, coaxially align a long handle, push through spring resistance, and engage a keyed lug and button.
comparisons.success_condition: The lug bottoms in its notch, the spring button protrudes through the window, and the assembled mop is released and still.
comparisons.reason: It tests alignment and forceful snap-latch insertion of two long parts, not maintaining an angular screw setting while tightening a concentric locknut.

comparisons.objective: Extinguish a nearby candle before safely packing a vase into a box.
comparisons.physical_skill: Place a bell snuffer over a wick without moving the chamberstick, then transfer and place a fragile vase.
comparisons.success_condition: The flame is extinguished before packing, the candle holder never exceeds movement limits, and the vase is upright, released, and still in the box.
comparisons.reason: This is hazard sequencing plus careful placement, with no adjustable threaded mechanism or retention-under-cycle requirement.

comparisons.objective: Candidate configures and locks a gripper motion limit; PR-2252 refits and latches a heavy range-hood baffle filter.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires seated driver/wrench coordination that prevents a screw setting from drifting during nut tightening; PR-2252 requires carrying an awkward slab, seating its bottom edge in a trough, swinging it flush, and operating a spring latch.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades target opening, lock retention, repeated motion, drift, hardware retention, and final clearance; PR-2252 grades trough engagement, flush seating, latch return over the filter, release, and one-second stability.
comparisons.reason: PR-2252’s placement-and-latching outcome does not test torque-coupled adjustment preservation or repeated functional retention; no material comparison rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Reorient an angle-grinder guard toward an operator and clamp it; the candidate calibrates and locks a robot-gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: The board task opens an over-centre lever, rotates a guard, and reclamps it while avoiding the disc; the candidate seats two concentric tools and counterholds screw torque during jam-nut tightening.
comparisons.success_condition: The guard must face the operator within 30°, have its lever flat, and leave the grinder nearly unmoved; the candidate must retain a 90° stop through three cycles with bounded drift and tool clearance.
comparisons.reason: Both preserve an angular setting after locking, but the guard task tests lever-mediated safety-guard positioning rather than coupled threaded adjustment and countertorque.

comparisons.objective: Sort colored cubes while responding to a high-level alarm by closing a tank inlet before overflow.
comparisons.physical_skill: Monitor a timed process, interrupt a sorting task, operate a sliding valve, and resume manipulation.
comparisons.success_condition: All cubes are correctly sorted and the valve is closed after the alarm but before overflow and remains closed; overflow scores zero.
comparisons.reason: Its tested difficulty is event-timed task switching and valve operation, not precision mechanical calibration and locknut counterholding.

comparisons.objective: Rotate a long parcel in confined space and push it into a bay; candidate configures a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coordinated opposing pushes for in-place carton rotation, followed by translation; no fastener engagement or counterholding.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires correct parcel orientation and placement without moving neighboring boxes; candidate requires a locked 90° setting retained through actuation.
comparisons.reason: The parcel task tests constrained whole-object reorientation, not coupled screw-and-jam-nut adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Pry a press-fit paint-tin lid free and place it safely; candidate sets and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Insert a screwdriver into a rim groove, lever successive lid regions, and reorient the tin; no simultaneous wrench/driver countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: Scores partial lid release, full removal, safe orientation, placement, and release; candidate scores angular accuracy and retained function after locking.
comparisons.reason: Tool use is shared, but distributed prying of a lid tests a different contact mechanism and outcome from preserving a threaded adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Rinse a glass on a push-down bar rinser and leave it draining on a mat.
comparisons.physical_skill: Invert and center a glass, depress a spring-loaded plate while maintaining coverage, then transport and place the glass rim-down.
comparisons.success_condition: The rinser is covered and depressed for 1.5 seconds and the glass is released, stable, and rim-down on the drip mat without unsafe spraying.
comparisons.reason: This tests spring-loaded appliance actuation and glass placement, unrelated to threaded setting preservation and jam-nut locking.

comparisons.objective: Install safety caps on exposed rebar stubs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Pick up bulky caps, coaxially align blind bores over bars, and push them down far enough to engage gripping fins.
comparisons.success_condition: All five bars have fully seated, retained caps and both robot tools remain clear for three seconds; dislodged caps revoke credit.
comparisons.reason: This is repeated axial press-fit insertion and retention, not rotational adjustment with coupled screw-and-nut countertorque or functional cycling.

comparisons.objective: Free a tote strap ring from a rake tine, then move the tote from shelf to table.
comparisons.physical_skill: Unhooking an articulated strap without dragging the rake, followed by bimanual tote transport.
comparisons.success_condition: Ring off every tine; rake remains safely on the shelf; tote upright, released, and still on the table.
comparisons.reason: Tests entanglement removal and transport, not precise screw adjustment, jam-nut counterlocking, or retained articulated cycling.

comparisons.objective: Place caplets in the correct pill-organizer cells and snap every lid shut.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold down a light organizer while lifting small catches, placing pills, and re-latching lids.
comparisons.success_condition: Exactly one caplet in Monday and Thursday, no dosing errors, all lids snapped, organizer released and stable.
comparisons.reason: Tests small-lid unlatching, placement, and snapping; it has no adjustable stop, coupled screw/nut locking, or setting-retention verification.

comparisons.objective: Magnetically attach a stylus to a tablet and lift the tablet from a flush tabletop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Magnetic face alignment, creation of thin-object grasp access, and attachment-preserving lift.
comparisons.success_condition: Stylus correctly attached and unsupported by a hand while the tablet is held at least 50 mm above the desk for five seconds.
comparisons.reason: Tests magnetic alignment and flat-object pickup rather than countertorque, locknut tightening, and repeatable stop-angle retention.

comparisons.objective: Form a two-bend 45-degree offset in tubing and place it on a template.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repositioning tube through a hand bender, making opposite irreversible bends, and compensating for springback.
comparisons.success_condition: Two acceptable bends, parallel ends at the specified offset, released on the template and still; over-bending or same-direction bends fail.
comparisons.reason: Tests material forming and springback across two bends, not adjustment of an existing mechanism followed by jam-nut locking and functional cycles.

comparisons.objective: Elicit a knee-jerk response with a reflex hammer and put the hammer down safely.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fast, accurately located impact followed by prompt lift-off and tool placement.
comparisons.success_condition: A sufficiently strong kick from a valid brisk tendon strike, then hammer released in its cup or on the bench and still.
comparisons.reason: Tests dynamic striking speed, impact location, and lift-off rather than coupled rotary adjustment and retention.

comparisons.objective: Deploy an attached folding support and leave a tablet standing for hands-free viewing.
comparisons.physical_skill: Manipulating thin hinged panels, coordinating an attached assembly, and transferring load to a stable support.
comparisons.success_condition: Tablet released near the required portrait tilt, supported by its edge and stand, and stable for five seconds.
comparisons.reason: Although both involve articulated motion and released verification, this tests support deployment and load transfer, not preserving a screw setting while locking a jam nut.

comparisons.objective: Press a weatherstrip-loaded door shut and throw its deadbolt.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual sustained door restraint while pinching and rotating a thumb-turn.
comparisons.success_condition: Bolt substantially extended into the strike while the door remains shut and stable for one second.
comparisons.reason: Shares generic stabilization-plus-turning, but tests maintaining door alignment against spring force while throwing a bolt, not concentric screw/nut countertorque, calibrated adjustment, or cycle retention.

comparisons.objective: Present a calibration checkerboard in the views needed for camera calibration, then return it to its rack.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual board handling with precise pose coverage, visibility control, and steady holds.
comparisons.success_condition: All positional, scale, and skew views detected; focal length recovered within tolerance; board returned, released, and still.
comparisons.reason: Tests multi-view visual target presentation and calibration observability, with no threaded setting or locking operation.

comparisons.objective: Pour an accurate 10 mL syrup dose while holding a cup level, then place both vessels; candidate adjusts a mechanical stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coordinated vessel holding, flow-rate control, and precise pour termination; no threaded adjustment or locking reaction.
comparisons.success_condition: Scores dose volume, spill, observability, placement, and settling; candidate scores locked opening angle and repeatable cycles.
comparisons.reason: Precision pouring and spill control are unrelated to two-tool setting preservation despite both requiring bimanual coordination.

comparisons.objective: Seat a close-fitting rigid box lid squarely over a product without wedging or damage; the candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2264 tests level multi-edge alignment and controlled telescoping insertion; the candidate tests driver/wrench seating, threaded regulation, counterholding, and articulated verification.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2264 grades lid height, centring, squareness, engagement, box stability, and release; the candidate grades opening angle, nut retention, cycle repeatability, drift, and clearance.
comparisons.reason: Close-fit lid placement and threaded stop calibration test different manipulation abilities and outcomes.

comparisons.objective: Move a heavy mortar to a marked area while keeping or restoring its loose pestle inside; the candidate configures a gripper mechanism.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2272 tests coordinated transport of a heavy container with an unstable loose load; the candidate tests precision tool seating, coupled screw/nut torque, and functional actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2272 requires target placement, pestle containment, stability, and robot clearance; the candidate requires a locked 90° setting retained over three cycles with low drift.
comparisons.reason: Managing a loose load during transport does not test preservation of a threaded calibration under locknut reaction.

comparisons.objective: Scan four groceries exactly once and relay them to a bagging shelf; the candidate adjusts and locks an industrial gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2276 tests barcode-facing reorientation, occlusion avoidance, handoff, and varied-object transport; the candidate tests concentric tool use and torque-controlled setting retention.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2276 awards each item only for one decode and released shelf placement, with drop and unpaid-item failures; the candidate grades angle accuracy, locking, repeated motion, drift, retention, and clearance.
comparisons.reason: The checkout task's tested ability is perception-guided item presentation and relay, not mechanical adjustment or countertorque.

comparisons.objective: Load washable blender components into a dishwasher while excluding the motor base.
comparisons.physical_skill: Semantic object selection and collision-safe placement of a jug and lid in a rack.
comparisons.success_condition: Jug and lid separately released and stable inside the rack; motor entry permanently fails the task.
comparisons.reason: Tests selective sorting and placement, not dexterous adjustment, counterlocking, or post-lock functional verification.

comparisons.objective: Remove a drone prop nut, replace the propeller, and retighten the nut; candidate adjusts and locks a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a freely rotating propeller while turning one nut, remove and insert parts, then tighten; candidate counterholds an adjustment screw while tightening its concentric jam nut.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires the nut to come off, the old propeller to be binned, the new one seated, and the nut tightened; candidate requires a 90° setting retained through three cycles.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest shared primitive of resisting rotation during nut turning, but propeller replacement does not test preserving an adjustable setting against jam-nut reaction or verifying retained articulated motion.

comparisons.objective: Unzip an antistatic bag, extract one 18650 cell, orient it in a holder, leave the other cell, and return the arms; the candidate adjusts and validates a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1302 tests zipper operation, selective extraction, cylindrical insertion, and polarity orientation; the candidate tests coaxial driver/wrench manipulation and locknut counterholding.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1302 grades unzip travel, extraction, seated upright polarity, the remaining cell, arm return, and one-second stillness; the candidate grades retained opening angle and repeated cycles.
comparisons.reason: Only the complete PR body was available—no task.json/spec, exact setup dimensions, or fidelity rubric—but its stated objective and numeric scoring are clearly unrelated to threaded stop locking.

comparisons.objective: Clamp an edge-glued panel with three clamps alternating above and below.
comparisons.physical_skill: Place a clamp, close multiple sliding jaws, regulate clamping force, and maintain panel alignment.
comparisons.success_condition: Joint closed and level with three snug alternating clamps; excessive force permanently fails; hands clear and assembly still.
comparisons.reason: Tests distributed force application and clamp layout, not locking a rotary adjustment without disturbing it or checking repeated actuator return.

comparisons.objective: Fit and hand-tighten a keyed oxygen regulator yoke on a cylinder; candidate sets and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Blind pin alignment, yoke seating, and holding the assembly square while turning a T-screw; no driver-held adjustment screw beneath a jam nut.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires pin insertion, washer alignment, clamp torque, release, and stability; candidate requires angular accuracy, lock retention, and repeated actuation.
comparisons.reason: Although both combine stabilization with screw tightening, the regulator tests keyed insertion and clamp formation rather than preserving a pre-set screw position during locknut tightening.

comparisons.objective: Tear a loaded shelf-ready tray's front panel off along its perforations without spilling or damaging the tray; the candidate calibrates and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1834 tests bimanual restraint plus direction-sensitive peeling and progressive fracture; the candidate tests precision threaded adjustment and countertorque with two tools.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1834 requires prescribed perforation separation, retained cans, limited tray motion, release, and stillness; the candidate requires angle accuracy, locked nuts, repeated cycles, and low drift.
comparisons.reason: Controlled perforation tearing of packaging is materially different from preserving a mechanical setpoint during jam-nut tightening.

comparisons.objective: Slit a carton's taped seam without damaging the product, then retract the cutter blade.
comparisons.physical_skill: Deploy a blade and control its angle, depth, and path over a long cut.
comparisons.success_condition: Tape completely slit, product and cardboard outside the tape undamaged, blade retracted, and carton not tipped.
comparisons.reason: Tests guarded cutting-depth control and tool-state restoration, not bimanual rotary counterlocking or repeated mechanism actuation.

comparisons.objective: Hand-guide a Franka arm to a service pose while correctly holding an enabling switch, then teach the pose; candidate mechanically configures a gripper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Continuous force-guiding of a seven-joint arm while maintaining a three-position safety control in its enable band.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires pose accuracy, correct button state, Teach actuation, collision avoidance, and clearance; candidate requires a locked opening angle retained over cycles.
comparisons.reason: Robot setup relevance is shared, but hand-guiding with an enabling device tests a different physical ability from mechanical stop adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Open a casement window to the last peg-stay hole and secure it there.
comparisons.physical_skill: Lift a stay clear of intermediate holes while moving the sash, then lower the correct hole over a pin.
comparisons.success_condition: Last hole captured on the pin, hands clear, sash and stay still; glass intrusion or an unsecured stay fails.
comparisons.reason: Tests coordinated articulated repositioning and hole-on-pin capture, not tool-driven screw adjustment or torque-preserving lockup.

comparisons.objective: Load an anaesthetic cartridge into a dental syringe and engage its harpoon safely.
comparisons.physical_skill: Orient and insert a fragile cartridge, align a small harpoon with a stopper, and apply bounded axial force.
comparisons.success_condition: Cartridge correctly oriented in the barrel, harpoon passes an aspiration test, syringe rests correctly, and excessive stopper travel never occurs.
comparisons.reason: Tests fragile insertion and controlled barb engagement rather than rotary setpoint adjustment, jam-nut locking, and repeated stop verification.

comparisons.objective: Separate the halves of a side-release buckle.
comparisons.physical_skill: Simultaneously depress two sprung tabs while restraining the light halves and pulling them apart.
comparisons.success_condition: Both tabs actuated and the male tongue fully withdrawn; falling off the table fails.
comparisons.reason: Tests concurrent latch release and extraction, with no adjustable setting, threaded countertorque, or retained-cycle outcome.

comparisons.objective: Install three culture-tube caps at their vented first detent rather than the sealed second detent.
